Title: Hartalega faces Q3 earnings pressure on softer ASPs, higher costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts expect Hartalega Holdings Bhd to report weaker quarter-on-quarter earnings in the third quarter of financial year 2027 (Q3 FY27), weighed down by the normalisation of average selling prices (ASPs) and a lag in passing higher raw material costs on to customers.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd expects near-term profitability to come under pressure from the normalisation of ASPs and delays in passing on higher raw material costs to customers, following earlier purchases at elevated prices, potentially squeezing margins.
"Over the medium term, Hartalega continues to expect persistent industry oversupply and ongoing pricing pressure from Chinese manufacturers to limit sector upside, broadly in line with our expectations.
"Consequently, the company remains focused on maintaining cost discipline and accelerating automation adoption to mitigate the impact of labour cost inflation," it said in a note.
Hartalega Holdings Bhd recorded a core net profit of RM28 million in Q2 FY27, bringing its first-half core net profit to RM99 million.
The first-half earnings accounted for 85 per cent of CIMB Securities' full-year forecast and 60 per cent of consensus estimates, exceeding expectations mainly due to higher-than-anticipated ASPs in Q2.
This was despite the partial impact of a weaker US dollar against the ringgit and a marginal one per cent year-on-year decline in sales volume.
"Following the results release, we raise our FY27 core net profit forecast for Hartalega by nine per cent to reflect stronger-than-expected ASPs.
"However, we trim our FY28 and FY29 core net profit forecasts by two and three per cent, respectively, to account for the impact of higher minimum wages, partially mitigated by efficiency gains arising from the company's manufacturing line upgrades and automation initiatives," CIMB Securities.
Meanwhile, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said Hartalega expects sales volume to rise 10 per cent quarter-on-quarter in Q3 FY27, following subdued customer purchases over the previous two quarters.
It said Hartalega had increased the ASPs of generic medical nitrile gloves (3.0 to 3.5 grams per piece) in October and November from September's low, with further price adjustments in December depending on movements in Brent crude oil prices.
"That said, we expect blended ASP in Q3 FY27 to be weaker QoQ, as Q2 FY26's realised prices were elevated by delayed shipments carrying the peak May pricing," it said.
However, HLIB does not expect the latest round of ASP increases to boost profit margins as significantly as in Q1 FY27.
"The key difference is the absence of a temporary tailwind that benefited Hartalega earlier: NBR shortages and cash deposit requirements from NBR suppliers, which temporarily forced smaller and mid-sized players to scale back production and helped alleviate the industry oversupply," HLIB said.
It said the current ASP increases are likely to support earnings mainly through the lagged impact of inventory costs, rather than a significant improvement in profit margins.
The firm said the roughly 19 per cent decline in Brent crude oil prices since Oct 30 could put pressure on margins in December, as higher-cost nitrile butadiene rubber inventories are used in production amid potentially lower ASPs and rising natural gas costs.
Looking ahead, HLIB expects Hartalega's earnings to weaken further in Q4 FY27, weighed down by continued moderation in oil prices into the first quarter of calendar year 2027 and a further natural gas tariff increase of about 10 per cent.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Hold" call on Hartalega with an unchanged target price of RM1.12, noting that the weaker near-term earnings outlook has largely been priced in.
Meanwhile, HLIB downgraded the company to "Sell" from "Hold" and lowered its target price to 80 sen from 97 sen, citing persistent structural oversupply and overly optimistic market expectations of margin expansion following the recent Brent crude oil price rally.

Title: Melaka polls: PH hopes for 75pc voter turnout, banks on outstation voters
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is targeting a voter turnout of at least 75 per cent in tomorrow's state election, five percentage points higher than the Election Commission's (EC) target.
The coalition is banking on outstation and young voters to help swing the contest in its favour.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the target was achievable, noting that nearly 30 per cent of the state's electorate comprised voters living outside Melaka, including those in the Klang Valley, southern states and overseas.
"Earlier this week, I met a young Melakan who flew all the way back from France just to cast his ballot, alongside others returning from New Zealand.
"Nobody paid them to come back. They did it out of a sense of responsibility for the state's future," he said at a press conference at PH's main operations centre here today.
The EC is targeting a 70 per cent voter turnout in the Melaka election. Its deputy chairman Dr Azmi Sharom said the commission hoped the public would show keen interest in voting, given that this was a state election rather than a by-election. (hyperlink: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1576666/melaka-polls-ec-targets-70-cent-voter-turnout)
Adly urged voters to plan their journeys early and check their polling details. He also reminded them to respect EC officials and security personnel to ensure a smooth voting process.
Adly, who is defending his Bukit Katil seat, also called on voters to reject race- and religion-based politics in favour of clean leadership.
Meanwhile, acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said the coalition remained focused on securing the 18 "hot seats" it had identified as crucial to forming the next state government.
PH is contesting 24 of the 28 state seats up for grabs in the election.
Adam said first-time voters aged 18 and above would play a decisive role in tomorrow's polls, citing studies indicating that 68 per cent of Melaka's youth prioritised transparency, integrity and good governance.
Responding to claims by rival coalitions that they could win 24 to 25 seats, he dismissed the projections as mere rhetoric.
"Everyone has their own targets. For us, there are no tailwinds blowing from the right, just hard work.
"On this final day, our candidates are revisiting voters to ensure no one is overlooked and that our core messages resonate," he said.
"Voting isn't just about who wins or loses; it is about protecting our home. Melakans have shown in past elections that they are brave enough to make bold choices, and we are confident they will make the right call tomorrow," he added.

Title: Indonesia faces renewed pressure to sustain investor confidence: analyst
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia faces renewed pressure to maintain investor confidence and economic stability after vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation, with his successor's credibility expected to play a crucial role in shaping market sentiment, an economist said.
Business and economic analyst Dr Muhammad Ramaditya said Indonesia's financial markets reacted differently to Gibran's resignation; the rupiah weakened amid political uncertainty, while domestic equities rallied as investors welcomed the prospect of a smoother political transition.
"On the currency side, political uncertainty triggered an immediate wave of risk aversion, pushing the rupiah down to a record low of Rp18,247 per US dollar. Conversely, domestic equities reacted with relief.
"The Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) actually rallied 2.66 per cent to close at 5,250.89, as stock investors viewed Gibran's voluntary step-down as a pressure valve that averted a prolonged, destabilising impeachment battle in Parliament," he told Bernama.
Gibran formally submitted his resignation letter to the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) on Thursday, amid legal developments concerning his educational qualifications, prompting the assembly to begin a selection process for a successor.
The MPR has up to 60 days to fill the vacancy. President Prabowo Subianto is required to nominate two candidates within 14 days of receiving a formal request from the assembly.
Although the broader economic consequences of Gibran's resignation have yet to become apparent, Ramaditya, who is also a lecturer at the University of Indonesia's Faculty of Administrative Sciences, said investors remained in a wait-and-see position, with much depending on the selection of his successor.
"If economic conditions worsen alongside political instability, it could lead to a crisis unless the situation is addressed quickly," he warned.
The political transition comes as Indonesia's capital market faces heightened scrutiny after global index provider MSCI announced plans to remove energy conglomerate Barito Pacific (BRPT) and Bumi Resources Minerals (BRMS) from its Global Standard Indexes, effective Dec 1, according to its latest review.
The changes are expected to leave just seven Indonesian companies in the MSCI Indonesia Index compared with 17 in April, based on MSCI's earlier index factsheet and Indonesian financial media reports.
The latest review follows MSCI's Oct 15 proposal to reclassify Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market amid concerns over ownership transparency and suspected coordinated trading, with a decision expected by June 2027.
Ramaditya said the credibility of Gibran's successor is critical to reassure investors in the political transition. This is particularly so, as Indonesia faces heightened scrutiny from MSCI over capital market governance and transparency.
"First and foremost, the successor must bring an unassailable legal, educational, and ethical track record to immediately reassure both domestic and international investors, especially at a time when currency markets are sensitive to governance questions and global index providers like MSCI are closely watching Indonesian market credibility," he said.
Beyond personal credibility, Ramaditya said the next vice-president will need to improve coordination across government agencies to address bottlenecks in state budget disbursement, infrastructure delivery and cooperation with regional administrations.
He said effective coordination will be essential to advancing Indonesia's economic priorities, including downstream industrialisation, energy transition and formal job creation, while ensuring that government spending translates into tangible economic benefits.
"A successful transition will require a vice-president who champions labour-intensive industries and eases friction for small businesses, all the while keeping the ruling coalition united without resorting to unbudgeted populist spending that could threaten Indonesia's fiscal discipline," he said.

Title: TVET cates record up to 99.1pct employment rate in 2025 - Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates recorded employment rates of up to 99.1 per cent in last year, with more graduates earning RM2,001 and above monthly.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the number of TVET graduates also increased from 133,594 in 2023 to 205,795 last year.
"Employment rates among TVET graduates ranged between 86.4 and 99.1 per cent across different qualification levels from 2023 to 2025.
"In 2025, advanced diploma and advanced certificate graduates recorded the highest employment rate at 99.1 per cent each, followed by first-degree graduates at 96.6 per cent, diploma graduates at 95.9 per cent and certificate graduates at 95.4 per cent," he said in a parliamentary written reply.
Zahid said more first-degree TVET graduates were earning RM2,001 and above monthly, with the figure rising from 62.5 per cent in 2023 to 76.9 per cent in 2025.
"For diploma graduates, the proportion increased from 23.2 per cent to 43.4 per cent, while certificate holders recorded an increase from 13 per cent to 26.2 per cent over the same period.
"This positive development reflects improving income prospects among TVET graduates and demonstrates its potential as a career pathway to improve living standards and economic mobility," he said.
He added that 125,864 TVET graduates had been recorded as at Sept 30 this year.

Title: Miti: No clearance granted to Megaspeed, Speedmatrix
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry clarifies that it has never given clearance or approval to Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd or its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, amid growing scrutiny over the movement of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips.
The clarification comes after Megaspeed and Speedmatrix were linked to international concerns over whether high-performance Nvidia chips brought into Malaysia may have been reexported to other countries, including China.
The ministry said visits to data centres where Speedmatrix operates were part of its routine monitoring of the sector and should not be interpreted as an endorsement or clearance of the companies.
Speedmatrix is a tenant at Malaysian data centres and brings in its own servers and AI chips for its operations.
The ministry said importing AI chips into Malaysia currently does not require a permit or licence.
However, since July 2025, companies seeking to export, reexport, transship or transit high-performance US AI chips from or through Malaysia must first obtain a permit from Miti under the Strategic Trade Act 2010.
The ministry is now working with the Customs Department to determine whether any chips brought into the country were subsequently reexported and if this complied with Malaysian law.
Providing false information relating to such goods is also a serious offence under the Customs Act 1967, it said.
The ministry said Malaysia will conduct its own independent checks based on local laws and available evidence, while working closely with authorities in Singapore and the United States to strengthen safeguards.
The case has drawn attention to Malaysia's growing role as a regional data centre hub.
Advanced AI chips have become increasingly sensitive because of US restrictions aimed at limiting China's access to high-end computing technology.
Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia chips, has faced scrutiny in the US and Singapore over possible breaches of export controls.
The company has denied wrongdoing.
Earlier reports said Malaysian authorities were prepared to examine whether Speedmatrix had breached local laws if evidence emerged that restricted chips had been improperly reexported.
The ministry also warned companies against misrepresenting their dealings with government agencies.
While Malaysia does not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries, it said companies operating here were expected to take such restrictions into account when conducting international business.
Malaysia welcomes investments in data centres and technology, the ministry said, but will not allow the country to be used to bypass export controls.
"The government will take stern action against any company found to have broken Malaysian law," it added.

Title: Kepong cop's attacker reported to have mental health issues
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The foreigner who attacked a policeman with a parang in Kepong on Wednesday was believed to have been experiencing mental health issues before the incident.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said investigations revealed that an acquaintance of the suspect had lodged a police report claiming that the man was mentally unstable and had been behaving aggressively at his home.
He said policemen, accompanied by personnel from the Fire and Rescue Department and the Health Ministry, went to the premises following the report.

Title: RM29.6b in housing financing approved under SJKP since 2021
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 114,834 housing financing applications worth RM29.6 billion were approved under the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) between 2021 and August 2026.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said 63,276 youths had benefited from the scheme, accounting for 50.9 per cent of its recipients as at Aug 31 this year.
"The achievement reflects SJKP's role in expanding access to housing financing, particularly for young people and first-time homebuyers who face difficulties meeting conventional financing requirements.
"The scheme helps first-time homebuyers, including youths, gig economy workers and individuals without fixed incomes, obtain housing financing through government guarantees of up to RM500,000," he said in a parliamentary written reply.
The scheme also takes into account different income sources and employment profiles, helping to reduce financing barriers for those who may not qualify under conventional lending requirements.
However, Nga said homeownership affordability also depended on individual income, property prices, existing financial commitments and credit eligibility.
Through the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, the government would continue to focus on providing affordable housing based on household income, actual demand and suitable development locations, he said.
The Housing and Local Government Ministry would also strengthen cooperation with state governments, housing agencies and private developers to identify potential new affordable housing developments.
"The government's priority is to ensure that young people not only have more housing options but are also able to own their first homes sustainably without taking on excessive financial burdens," he said.

Title: Trump's interactions with ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in the spotlight
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's close ties with billionaire Jensen Huang ​have come under renewed scrutiny after revelations about the former Nvidia chief executive officer's (CEO) affairs, including with a businesswoman alleged to be a spy for China.
Trump has said he was "amazed" after the revelations concerning one of his closest allies in Silicon Valley. Huang resigned on November 12 and faces an FBI probe and congressional hearings.
Over the past two years, Huang has voiced support for the Trump administration's AI agenda and met the Republican leader many times as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market and lobbied for looser restrictions on Chinese access to Nvidia's sophisticated AI chips.
Democratic and Republican lawmakers have called to halt exports of advanced AI chips to China. Huang and the White House have argued that continuing US sales to China would keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology.
Here is a timeline of some publicly known interactions and meetings between Huang and Trump since the Republican leader returned to the White House in January 2025:
JANUARY 2025:
Trump met Huang during the first month of his return to the White House, casting the interaction as a good meeting.
JULY 2025:
The then-Nvidia CEO met Trump at the White House before Huang's visit to China.
Later in the month, Trump gave a shout-out to Huang as he spoke and signed executive orders at an AI summit.
"Jensen, will you stand up? What a job, what a job you've done," Trump remarked. "He's a great guy too."
AUGUST 2025:
Huang met Trump at the White House as the Trump administration and Nvidia engaged in talks over allowing advanced AI chip sales to China.
SEPTEMBER 2025:
Huang joined Trump during a state visit to Britain.
NOVEMBER 2025:
Huang attended a US-Saudi Arabia investment forum in Washington during the first visit of Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to the US capital since 2018. Huang talked about the future of AI at the event.
DECEMBER 2025:
Trump praised Huang when the then-Nvidia CEO visited Washington and met the Republican leader, who said the chip executive was aware of where he stood on export controls.
Huang was in the US capital that day to meet lawmakers and told them that state-by-state US regulations would slow the progress of AI development.
JANUARY 2026:
The Trump administration began allowing some exports of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China on a case-by-case basis but it did not lift the restrictions applying to organisations that Washington had put on a trade restriction list.
MARCH 2026:
In late March, the White House announced Huang as part of a 13-member council formally called the "President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology" to weigh in on AI policy and other issues.
MAY 2026:
Huang was among a delegation of tech CEOs who joined Trump during his visit to China to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping as the Republican leader aimed to urge Beijing to "open up" to US business.
Trump, in a last-minute addition to his May trip to China, asked Huang to join him. Huang was spotted boarding Air Force One during a refuelling stop in Alaska en route to Beijing.
SEPTEMBER 2026:
As the Trump administration and AI companies faced increasing scrutiny over risks posed by advanced AI, Trump said on September 29 that Huang was among a number of AI CEOs who signed a voluntary safety pact and backed data center expansion.
Huang met Trump at the White House that day along with a number of tech executives. Trump, who had argued previously that the US ​does ⁠not need new AI-specific regulations, said the pact was "morally binding", prompting criticism that it did not lay out consequences for non-compliance.
In the previous week, Huang attended a high-profile state dinner for Xi at the White House when the Chinese leader met Trump.
In mid-September, Huang addressed AI safety concerns during a summit in Los Angeles. He took a phone call from Trump during the event and put him on speaker for the audience. During the roughly five-minute call, Trump called AI safety fears a "hoax."
OCTOBER 2026:
In early October, Trump awarded the National Medal of Science, the United States' highest honour for scientists and engineers, to Huang and some other tech industry leaders.
The same day Trump gave him the award, the president disclosed buying up to US$1.6 million and selling up to US$1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer of 2026.
The Washington Post reported in mid-October that Nvidia committed US$25 million for Trump's planned White House ballroom.
NOVEMBER 2026:
Trump said on November 9 that he spoke to the then-Nvidia boss after the affair between Huang and Alice Huang - an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, whom US authorities suspected to be a Chinese spy - became public.
Trump said the tech billionaire told him he had no idea that the woman was a spy and that Trump believed him.
'I asked him that question: "Did you have any idea that she was a spy?" 'He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,' and I really believe him," Trump told a White House briefing.
"I know the FBI is looking into it," Trump said. "I think that he'll be in good shape."
When asked about Huang's resignation on November 12, Trump said in a podcast interview that it was "sad" while describing him as a "tremendous talent."
"I spoke to him yesterday (November 11); he is going through hell," Trump said in the podcast.
The New York Times later reported Trump called him on November 10 and asked him to fight for his job.

Title: Digital Infrastructure Bill to be tabled next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Digital Infrastructure Bill (Data Centre) is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat next year.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the bill was in its final stages of drafting and aimed to strengthen the security, resilience and governance of data centres as critical national digital infrastructure.
He said the framework would adopt an all-hazards approach, covering cybersecurity threats, system failures, operational disruptions, natural disasters, physical risks and supply chain vulnerabilities.
"This includes an emphasis on preparedness, disaster recovery and business continuity to minimise the impact of disruptions on the national economy," Gobind said in a written parliamentary reply.
He was responding to Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi), who asked about the ministry's plans and timeline for introducing the proposed bill.
Gobind said the country's growing reliance on digital infrastructure, particularly data centres, made a dedicated legal framework necessary to ensure uninterrupted public services and economic activities.
"The importance of digital infrastructure is reflected in the information and communications technology (ICT) and e-commerce sectors, which contributed 23.5 per cent to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) in 2025.
"Approved digital investments also totalled RM385.71 billion between 2021 and June this year," he said.
He said the bill would undergo policy and legal coordination before being finalised and tabled for consideration and debate in Parliament.
Once passed and enforced, the ministry would coordinate the implementation of the regulatory framework to ensure compliance with prescribed security, resilience and operational continuity standards.

Title: PublicInvest sets 22 sen fair value on Yes Group, sees 17pct profit growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) has assigned a fair value of 22 sen to newly listed Yes Group Management Bhd.
The valuation reflects the company's expansion into Europe, talent development initiatives and growing Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) business, which are expected to drive earnings growth.
Analyst Lee Siao Ping said the company's expansion plans, including the establishment of Yes Academy and the growth of its MM2H business, were expected to support a three-year net profit compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 17 per cent.
"We forecast Yes Group's net profit to reach RM12 million by financial year 2029 (FY29), supported by its European expansion, talent development initiatives and growth in the MM2H segment," he said in a note.
PublicInvest derived the fair value based on an about 12 times price-to-earnings ratio (PER) applied to calendar year 2027 forecast earnings per share, representing a 10 per cent discount to its local listed peer's around 13.5 times PER.
Lee said the discount reflected Yes Group's relatively smaller market capitalisation and business scale.
The company's European expansion involves establishing a regional office near London Heathrow Airport and progressively acquiring vehicles to support incentive travel engagements and ad hoc ground transportation services.
"The UK ground transportation industry caters to business and premium leisure travellers through chauffeur-driven services, with demand supported by growing overseas business visits and airport passenger traffic, particularly for airport transfer," he said.
Lee said the establishment of Yes Academy would help develop industry talent, strengthen manpower capacity and support the scalability of the company's meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) operations.
The company also plans to expand its MM2H segment by leveraging its existing MICE expertise and operational capabilities to grow its customer base.
"Long-term growth is further supported by sustained demand for customised incentive travel and MICE solutions, underpinned by Yes' established track record, diversified clientele and resilient competitive positioning," he said.
Yes Group completed 403 incentive travel engagements between FY23 and FY26, with repeat private sector corporate customers accounting for 40.4 per cent of its clientele.
As of Oct 9, the company had an unbilled order book of RM34.6 million, comprising entirely customised incentive travel engagements.
Of the total, RM34.4 million involved overseas destinations, particularly Europe at RM16.1 million and Asia at RM15.6 million.
PublicInvest said RM34 million of the unbilled order book was expected to be recognised in FY27, with the remaining RM600,000 in FY28.
Malaysia's MICE industry is supported by economic growth, rising corporate expenditure and increasing demand for incentive travel to motivate and retain employees.
Government support through tax incentives and business events initiatives, including MyTripleE 3.0, is also expected to strengthen Malaysia's position as a regional business events destination.
On its financial position, PublicInvest said Yes Group's gross gearing ratio was expected to improve to 0.01 times post-listing, from 0.02 times, following an increase in total equity.
Its gearing ratio had declined from 0.90 times in FY24 to 0.02 times in FY26, supported by higher retained earnings from consistent profitability and lower borrowings following the full settlement of several term loans and a hire purchase facility.
Yes Group does not currently have a fixed dividend policy.

Title: Selangor sees increase in flood victims, Perak records drop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood victims at relief centres in Selangor has increased, while it has decreased in Perak, as of 8am today.
In SELANGOR, the number of victims still being accommodated in seven relief centres has increased to 1,248 victims from 338 families compared to 1,144 victims from 318 families yesterday evening.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, the PPS at SK Dato' Maharaja Lela accommodated 393 victims, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (281), SK Parit Mahang (318), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (71) and Kafa Integrasi Hidayah (122).
In addition, Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam accommodated 50 victims, while Dewan Orang Ramai Hulu Bernam, in Hulu Selangor, accommodated 13 victims.
Meanwhile, in PERAK, the number of flood victims in the Hilir Perak district decreased to 288 people from 83 families, compared with 301 people from 87 families yesterday evening.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the PPS at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House accommodated 268 victims from 78 families, while 20 people from five families are still taking shelter at Dewan MPTI Langkap.
According to the Drainage and Irrigation Department, the water level in Sungai Kurau at the Bukit Merah Reservoir recorded a warning level with a reading of 9.14m, while the Malaysian Meteorological Department predicted that storms and rain are expected to occur in the afternoon and evening in several districts in the state, including Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar and Kinta.

Title: Anwar explains move to bring Najib's case before Pardons Board in 2023
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he brought Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application before the Pardons Board in 2023 to ensure that his right to seek a pardon was not denied.
He said every prisoner had the right to submit an appeal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for consideration under the Federal Constitution.
"I want to explain why I brought Datuk Seri Najib's case to the Pardons Board in 2023. As prime minister, I could not bear to be seen as having treated anyone unjustly.
"Under our Federal Constitution, every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for consideration. If I had not allowed him to do so, it would have been tantamount to denying him that right," he said at the Pesta Melaka, Rumah Kita programme at Taman Melaka Perdana here last night.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, said his decision had nevertheless drawn criticism from those who accused him of betraying his principles in the fight against corruption.
He said his responsibility as prime minister was to ensure that the application was submitted for consideration, while the decision on whether to grant a pardon rested with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"If I had not done it, I would have been accused of betrayal. When I did it, I was still accused of betrayal. What is this?" he said.
Anwar also said supporting documents, including medical reports, prison records and reports on former prime minister's conduct, had been submitted as part of the application process.
He stressed that this did not mean the government was compromising its stance on fighting corruption and abuse of power.

Title: Melaka polls: EC targets 70 per cent voter turnout
Article:
JASIN: The Election Commission is targeting a 70 per cent voter turnout in the Melaka election tomorrow.
Its deputy chairman Dr Azmi Sharom said the commission hoped the public would show keen interest in voting, given that this was a state election rather than a by-election.
He also advised voters to cast their ballots early to avoid any inconvenience, particularly with rain forecast in some areas tomorrow.
"Voters are advised to come early or bring an umbrella in case it rains.
"Even if it rains, I hope the public will still turn out to vote, as that is what matters most," he told reporters after inspecting polling preparations at Dewan Platinum, Politeknik Melaka, for the Merlimau constituency here today.
On other matters, Azmi said the EC would continue using the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system to collect and display voter attendance data in real time.
He said the system allowed the public, political analysts and other interested parties to obtain the latest information on the number of voters who had turned up at polling centres.
"This system allows voter attendance data to be obtained in real time, and the public can visit the EC website to check the number of voters who have turned out.
"The information is useful not only to the EC but also to political analysts and other interested parties.
"Previously, voter turnout figures were updated hourly, but this system allows the information to be accessed in real time," he said.
He said election workers had so far adapted well to the system, which he described as user-friendly and relatively straightforward.
Azmi said the use of OCR-VA would not have a significant impact on the time taken to vote or compromise the secrecy of voters' ballots.
"We will continue using it as part of efforts to modernise the country's voting system.
"I also believe the system does not compromise ballot secrecy in any way or have a significant impact on the time voters take to cast their ballots," he said.
He also reminded voters to check their polling centres and voting streams through MySPR before heading out to vote tomorrow.
He said checking the details in advance would help voters complete the process more smoothly upon arrival at their polling centres and avoid confusion over where they should cast their ballots.
Voters without internet access can check their details at counters provided at polling centres.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RHB keeps "Buy" on Johor Plantations, cuts target price to RM2.00
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Research has maintained its 'Buy' recommendation on Johor Plantations Group Bhd (JPG), lowering its target price to RM2.00 from RM2.20 following its third-quarter earnings recovery.
The research firm said the revised target price represents an upside potential of 11.1 per cent from its market price of RM1.80.
In a note, RHB Research said JPG's third-quarter financial year 2026 core profit doubled quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), supported by higher fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production and lower unit costs.
Core profit rose 100.4 per cent QoQ to RM176.9 million, although it declined 13 per cent year-on-year (YoY), representing 70 per cent and 63 per cent of RHB Research's full-year and consensus estimates, respectively.
"We deem the results in line, as seasonally higher fourth-quarter financial year 2026 FFB output should support earnings, partly offset by softer crude palm oil (CPO) average selling prices (ASP) QoQ," it said.
The research house said FFB output increased 35.6 per cent QoQ, while the 12.6 per cent YoY decline reflected the seasonal crop cycle.
It added that improved weather conditions drove the recovery, although cumulative production remained weaker, with nine-month financial year 2026 FFB output down 11.8 per cent YoY.
"That said, the dry weather is still one of the key production drags, as seen in the weak year-to-date output.
"Nonetheless, management is confident that financial year 2026 FFB output will surpass the 1 million tonnes mark," it said.
For CPO, JPG recorded an ASP of RM4,683 per tonne in the third quarter of financial year 2026, up 0.8 per cent QoQ and 6.6 per cent YoY.
RHB Research said JPG secured premium pricing for its entire financial year 2026 output, with 70 per cent under identity preserved at RM200 to RM250 per tonne.
The remaining 30 per cent was under mass balance, fetching a premium of RM100 to RM150 per tonne.
However, CPO unit costs increased 10.9 per cent YoY to RM2,557 per tonne, driven by higher diesel prices, fertiliser prices and maintenance costs.
The research house consequently raised its financial year 2026 unit cost assumption to reflect the higher operating expenses. It also expects fertiliser requirements for financial year 2027 to push costs up by 15 per cent YoY.
"Overall, we trim financial year 2026 to financial year 2028 earnings by 2.9 per cent, 8.4 per cent, and 6.4 per cent after imputing for higher unit costs and lower palm kernel ASP premium," it said.
Despite the earnings adjustments, RHB Research said JPG's strong environmental, social and governance credentials continued to support its ability to command premium selling prices.
It added that the group's upcoming Integrated Sustainable Palm Oil Complex would further strengthen its downstream operations and support its transition into a fully integrated plantation group.
RHB Research expects the complex to begin commercial operations progressively in the first half of 2027, supporting JPG's transition into a fully integrated plantation group.

Title: New Zealand home prices fall in October, sales cool on cost pressures
Article:
SYDNEY: New Zealand home prices slipped in October as higher living costs and a weak job market weighed on buyer sentiment, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Friday.
Seasonally adjusted median house prices fell 0.7 per cent from September and were down 3.4 per cent from a year earlier, REINZ data showed.
National home sales were down more than 10 per cent from a month earlier and slumped 23 per cent from a year earlier, as the usual spring lift in sales did not emerge and properties took slightly longer to sell than they did a year prior.
"October's data shows a market that remains measured," said REINZ chief executive Lizzy Ryley.
"Greater choice is allowing buyers to assess their options carefully, while our members observed a measured approach among some vendors and buyers in the lead-up to the general election."
New Zealanders are facing weeks of uncertainty over who will govern the country after a general election on November 7, with the current coalition holding a slim majority. But a potentially decisive slice of votes has yet to be counted.
Some buyers and vendors may continue to wait for greater clarity until the next government is formed, though REINZ members expect the market to remain steady in the near term. And they hope sales activity will build up before the summer holidays.
A slight easing of inflation in the September quarter and the central bank's surprise decision to hold rates on October 28 may improve sentiment, "but it may take time for these signals to flow through to confidence and activity," Ryley said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Holiday rental boom squeezes out residents in Spain's Malaga
Article:
MALAGA: Carlos Carrera Lopez has long lived in central Malaga but fears his neighbourhood in the southern Spanish city is slowly disappearing as holiday rentals and mass tourism drive residents out.
"We are fighting to ensure this neighbourhood remains inhabited," the 53-year-old doctor, who heads the Old Town residents' association, told AFP, warning of a "mass exodus" caused by mounting tourist pressure.
"The very existence of the neighbourhood is at stake because residents are being forced out," he said. "How is it that we can no longer live in our own city?"
The same trend is playing out across Spain, fuelling protests and a general strike over housing affordability, as the issue became a key battleground ahead of an early general election on November 29.
Opinion polls suggest the conservative opposition is well placed to unseat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who has been in office since 2018.
Now one of the country's symbols of mass tourism, Malaga, with a population of around 600,000, welcomed a record 1.83 million visitors in 2025.
In some streets of the port city, nearly one in two homes is used for short-term tourist accommodation, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE).
It had more than 8,000 tourist apartments last year, up 40 per cent from 2020, making it Spain's second-largest market for this type of accommodation, behind Madrid but ahead of Barcelona.
- 'Unsustainable' -
Although tourist rentals account for only a relatively small share of the city's housing stock, they have added to pressure on rents, which have more than doubled over the past decade.
Spain's average gross monthly salary is about 2,460 euros (US$2,730), while renting a 50-square-metre apartment in Malaga cost an average of 835 euros in October, according to property portal Idealista.
"It's unsustainable!" said Francisco Lopez, 52. He runs a food bank in Malaga and laments the gradual disappearance of neighbourhood life, replaced by a constant stream of cleaners carrying bags of sheets to prepare holiday apartments for new guests.
"The past eight or 10 years have been horrible. It's been a real cancer!" he told AFP.
Two months ago, Lopez was forced to leave the flat he had rented for 16 years. He suspects his landlord intends to turn it into a tourist rental.
A few streets away, Monica Reino has lived with her family for seven years near the emblematic Plaza de la Merced, where Pablo Picasso was born.
Every day, she watches a steady stream of tourists dragging suitcases through narrow streets lined with souvenir shops, luggage lockers and key safes for holiday apartments advertised on platforms such as Airbnb.
"Every year it gets worse," said Reino, 56, explaining that half of the 20 flats in her building are now tourist apartments.
- 'Find a balance' -
Many residents welcome the major transformation Malaga has undergone since Francisco de la Torre of the conservative Popular Party became mayor in 2000.
Run-down central neighbourhoods have been renovated, while a pedestrian waterfront overlooking the Mediterranean has helped reshape the city.
Malaga has also sought to bolster its cultural appeal with new museums, including an outpost of Paris's Centre Pompidou modern art institution, which opened in 2015.
"We have gone from being a provincial city to a major metropolis," Carmen Casero Navarro, Malaga's deputy mayor for urban planning, told AFP.
Standing outside the city hall, an imposing neo-Baroque building overlooking the port, she acknowledged tensions caused by the proliferation of tourist apartments. But she also stressed the economic opportunities generated by the sector.
Tourism is a major industry in Malaga, she said: the sector employs around 50,000 people locally, according to official data.
Data supplied to AFP by AirDNA, a firm specialising in short-term rental market analysis, showed that properties listed on Airbnb, Booking.com and Vrbo in Malaga generated average gross revenue of 35,000 euros for their owners over the past 12 months. They put the average nightly rate at 142 euros.
The city council, which is working to create 5,000 social housing units, approved a reform of its urban development plan in July, suspending the granting of new tourist rental licences for three years.
The goal is to "find a balance", said Casero Navarro.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US existing home sales fall to lowest level since 2010
Article:
NEW YORK: Sales of previously owned US homes dropped to a more than 16-year low in October due to the drag from higher lending rates, a US realtors association said Thursday.
Sales fell in October by 8.8 per cent year-over-year to 3.75 million on a seasonally adjusted annual basis, according to estimates from the National Association of Realtors (NAR).
"Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023, said NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun.
"As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010."
The rate for a 30-year mortgage, a common mechanism for home purchases in the United States, is currently 7.18 per cent, according to mortgage finance giant Freddie Mac.
The lending rate topped the symbolically important six per cent level in February, before the start of the US-Israel strikes on Iran, which lifted energy prices and exacerbated overall inflation.
The median home price increased 0.4 per cent from one year ago to US$416,700 in October, while total housing inventory rose 4.6 per cent.
"Based on the current underwhelming home sales pace at a time of consistent job growth, there could be sizable pent-up demand if mortgage rates decline," Yun said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress
Article:
NEW YORK: SpaceX and Tesla are progressing in their merger negotiations, and a deal could be announced as early as December, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
The proposed merger would unify Elon Musk's AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate roof, though it faces steep regulatory hurdles over SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's reliance on China.
Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that a merger with Tesla would be "a good idea" and confirmed the companies had formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a union.
SpaceX and Tesla could not be immediately reached for comment on the report. As of last close, SpaceX had a market cap of about US$1.90 trillion, while Tesla is valued at around US$1.55 trillion.
The companies have also discussed a scenario in which the announcement slips into early 2027, the report said.
SpaceX and Tesla also have a chip manufacturing joint venture, Terafab. The JV should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year and aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028, Musk said on the call.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Inflation, legal system abuse cost liability insurers up to US$337bil in past decade
Article:
WASHINGTON: Auto and general liability insurers in the US incurred up to US$337 billion in additional losses from 2016 to 2025 because of inflation and legal system abuse, according to new research from the Insurance Information Institute.
Triple-I said that the additional losses were between 16 per cent and 19.6 per cent of total booked losses.
The property and casualty not-for-profit's research compares expected losses with actual losses to estimate the additional liability costs in a methodology developed with the Casualty Actuarial Society.
"The report's findings reinforce the need to address excessive litigation costs and promote a balanced legal environment that supports fair compensation for injured parties without imposing unnecessary costs on everyone else," Sean Kevelighan, chief executive officer (CEO) of Triple-I, said.
In personal auto liability, bodily injury claim severity is up 62.4 per cent compared with before the pandemic. Inflation has added up to US$120.1 billion in losses and cost containment expenses, or 10.8 per cent of booked losses.
In commercial auto, additional costs accounted for up to US$86 billion, or up to 34 per cent of booked losses. The research found that claim severity went up 8.2 per cent annually from 2016 to 2025, even as claim frequency returned to pre-pandemic levels.
Triple-I said that commercial auto "shows the strongest actuarial evidence of rising inflation among all lines", with economic inflation not surpassing claim severity since 2008. Commercial auto insurers have also been posting underwriting losses for years.
Product liability saw increasing inflation in 33.6 per cent of booked losses, with claim severity increasing at an annual rate of 22.8 per cent since 2016.
Other liability categories saw additional costs of up to US$125 billion, or up to 36.8 per cent of booked losses.
"Until claim severity growth decelerates broadly across these lines, insurers should expect continued upward pressure on liability premiums, leaving consumers with the prospect of ever-rising premiums," the report said.
​Triple-I on October 30 said US tort costs nearly doubled between 2014 and 2023, rising from US$299.7 billion to US$579.7 billion and significantly outpacing economic growth, in an analysis that drew on a US Chamber Institute for Legal Reform report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bollywood bolsters security as underworld fears return
Article:
MUMBAI: It sounds like a Bollywood thriller, but a spate of shootings and extortion threats targeting Mumbai's stars has sent the industry scrambling for bodyguards, reviving memories of the underworld's grip on cinema in the 1990s.
From gunshots to cash demands, the incidents have unsettled the Indian industry, decades after police crackdowns weakened the criminal gangs once deeply embedded in the multi-billion-dollar business.
Police have linked the latest violence to the gang of Lawrence Bishnoi, a convicted Indian gangster accused by US prosecutors of directing a global criminal network from behind bars.
"Stars are moving around with bodyguards on either side," actor and security agency owner Ronit Roy said.
"There has been a sharp increase in demand... Requests have expanded beyond just lead actors to include family members and children."
Author S. Hussain Zaidi, a former investigative journalist, said opportunistic criminals were exploiting the notoriety of established gangsters.
"Some desperadoes are opening fire in the air to scare the industry and spread fear," Zaidi told AFP.
"And they have succeeded – as people have started believing that the mafia-dominated 1990s era is back."
The latest incidents include gunfire targeting actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai in October, and an alleged US$600,000 extortion demand against actor Tusshar Kapoor.
Police have arrested 13 people under organised crime laws in connection with the October shooting, alleging it was intended to extort money, establish gang dominance and spread fear.
Police said there had also been surveillance of other prominent figures.
They have named Anil Pandit, an alleged Bishnoi gang member, as wanted in connection with the shooting.
Darkest periods
Anxiety reverberating across the industry has spilled into public view.
Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan recently greeted fans from behind a bulletproof enclosure outside his Mumbai home during his customary Sunday appearance, while security was beefed up around actor Shah Rukh Khan's home for his birthday.
But Zaidi said the major gangsters of the 1990s were now dead, imprisoned or inactive.
"The only gangster we hear of these days is Lawrence Bishnoi and even he is in jail, so there is no way that any local Mumbai-based gangster has control over the city," he said.
The late 1990s and early 2000s were among Bollywood's darkest periods, when criminal syndicates used threats, extortion and violence to influence film financing, casting and distribution.
They included Dawood Ibrahim, a UN-sanctioned fugitive accused of involvement in the 1993 Mumbai bombings that killed 257 people, and his former lieutenant-turned-rival Chhota Rajan, who is behind bars in India.
Producers were pressured to pay protection money, surrender business interests and bow to gangsters' demands.
The underworld's influence waned as police intensified operations, strengthened by laws passed in 1999 targeting organised crime, while the growth of corporate financing further reduced gangsters' influence over the film business.
'We will kill you'
Rajiv Rai, director of the hit thriller "Gupt", received extortion demands and threatening calls in the late 1990s before eventually leaving India for Britain.
"I was the victim in the 1990s, the world knows," he told AFP.
Watching the latest incidents unfold, Rai said the motives were harder to decipher.
Bishnoi's gang has been linked to threats against Salman Khan, reportedly over allegations that the Bollywood star had hunted blackbuck antelopes in 1998.
The animals are revered by the Bishnoi community, a Hindu sect whose faith places strong emphasis on wildlife protection.
Indian authorities have also accused gang members of opening fire outside Khan's Mumbai home and of involvement in the killing of Baba Siddique, a prominent politician with close ties to the film industry, in 2024.
After the October shooting targeting Shroff, a social media post and audio message attributed to a Bishnoi gang associate reportedly claimed responsibility, citing the actor's closeness to Khan.
"In the 1990s, we knew their agenda... ransom money," Rai said.
"Now they are calling and saying if you are Salman's friend, we will kill you... now what kind of agenda is this?"
Ahmed Ali, a crime journalist, said he believed that "many of these seem to be prank calls, to cash in on the situation that Bishnoi has created".
Producer Boney Kapoor, who was targeted by underworld figures over a dispute involving overseas distribution rights for his 1997 Salman Khan film "Judwaa", believes the latest wave of violence will be "short-lived".
"I don't feel that kind of fear," he said. "But one has to be cautious, these shootings can't be ignored."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mercedes to halt German investments, mulling plant closures
Article:
FRANKFURT: Struggling German carmaker Mercedes-Benz announced Thursday it will halt all investment in Germany and is mulling plant closures, underlining the woes facing the country's automotive sector.
Like its German peers, Mercedes has been battered by Chinese competition and high costs and last month became the third big German carmaker to cut its outlook for the year.
Its management has been locked in talks with staff representatives to find ways to reduce costs, but with little sign of negotiations were making progress, the manufacturer signalled a harder line.
"The executive board has jointly decided to halt all further investments in German sites," said board member Michael Schiebe in an interview posted on the company's intranet and sent to AFP.
Management was unable to see any way forward on finding a deal with unions "despite numerous intensive discussions", he said.
"We are now forced to carefully examine which German sites we would have to close if we cannot achieve a change in the cost structure."
Schiebe stressed, however, that management still hoped for a breakthrough in talks and that "we want the next generations of vehicles to also be built at our German locations."
There was nevertheless the possibility that "our new products will only be manufactured abroad," he said.
The powerful IG Metall union is currently demanding a pay rise of five per cent in wage negotiations with the company.
In the same document published on Thursday, another board member, Britta Seeger, called the union's demand "totally excessive".
"Such an increase would further drive up labour costs, already high in Germany, when they are already far too high in international comparison," she argued.
The company wants to implement a "productivity offensive" to drive down costs, including an increase in working hours for no extra pay, but here too there has been no agreement with the unions.
"These are uncomfortable topics but it is part of our job as the board to raise them if we want to change things," said Seeger.
Auto sector analyst Ferdinand Dudenhoeffer said that Thursday's news was indicative of the fact that Germany's car industry is in "its biggest crisis since its inception."
Mercedes' announcement was in itself "not a surprise". Dudenhoeffer said, noting that the company had been "stressing for months how difficult the situation is at its German sites."
"Without a fundamental realignment of the cost structure in Germany, the automotive industry here will simply die out," he said.
Last month Mercedes-Benz revised its profit outlook down to 5.8 billion euros (US$6.5 billion), on a par with 2025. It had previously foreseen an increase of at least 15 per cent.
BMW and Volkswagen had both already cut their guidance for the year after sluggish demand combined with cut-throat competition from Chinese rivals such as BYD and Xiaomi ate into profits.
Volkswagen plans to have cut 120,000 jobs globally by the end of the decade in what is the largest restructuring in automotive history, eclipsing the 50,000 jobs lost after the bankruptcy of General Motors in 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US starts 2027 fiscal year with record October budget deficit of US$404bil
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US government started the 2027 fiscal year with a US$404 billion budget deficit for October, a record for the month and an increase of US$120 billion or 42 per cent from the year-earlier period, as receipts shrank and outlays grew sharply, the Treasury Department said on Thursday.
The record October deficit marks another fiscal setback for Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent after the Treasury reported a full-year fiscal 2026 deficit of nearly US$2 trillion, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years.
Bessent has set a goal to reduce the deficit to 3.0 per cent of US GDP, but the 2026 budget gap was estimated at 6.2 per cent of GDP, up from 5.8 per cent for fiscal 2025.
October 2026 receipts fell by US$35 billion, or 9.0 per cent, to US$369 billion, due partly to a 39 per cent drop in net customs collections to US$19.2 billion from US$31.3 billion in October 2025, when President Donald Trump's global tariff revenues reached their peak.
October individual non-withheld tax receipts fell by US$29 billion, or 36 per cent, to US$51 billion from the year ago period, when they were swelled by tax payments after the expiration of delayed filing deadlines for Californians affected by wildfires in early 2025.
After calendar-related adjustments made because benefit payments for November were shifted into October for both fiscal years, the Treasury said the adjusted deficit would have been $285 billion, an increase of US$94 billion, or 49 per cent, from the year-ago period.
FARM, MILITARY, INTEREST OUTLAYS
But the reported October outlays came to a record for that month of US$773 billion, up US$84 billion, or 12 per cent, from year-ago levels.
The outlay increases were driven in part by a US$14 billion, or 80 per cent, increase in US Department of Agriculture spending due to farm relief payments and a US$28 billion, or 30 per cent, increase in military spending, representing an October payment to military trust funds that was delayed by last year's government shutdown, along with increases spread across operations, maintenance and procurement.
Gross interest on the federal debt also rose US$11 billion, or 11 per cent, from the previous October to US$115 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's BrahMos missile acquisition remains at exploratory stage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's proposed acquisition of India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile remains at the exploratory stage, with no decision made on the procurement.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the proposal was first raised during preliminary government-level discussions in conjunction with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's official visit to India in September.
"Any potential acquisition would require a comprehensive technical assessment by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), particularly on the missile's compatibility and integration with its existing Su-30MKM fighter jets.
"The assessment would cover operational requirements, compatibility with existing platforms, systems integration, upgrade requirements and life-cycle costs," he said in a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Seri Ikmal Hisham Abdul Aziz (PN-Tanah Merah).
Khaled added that integrating the BrahMos missile with the Su-30MKM would also involve detailed technical scrutiny, including aircraft modifications, testing and validation.
"Such processes would typically take a considerable amount of time before the capability could become fully operational," he said.
It was reported that Malaysia was in exploratory discussions to acquire the BrahMos system as part of broader efforts to strengthen defence and strategic cooperation with India.
In an interview with Indian broadcaster NDTV, Anwar said the
potential acquisition had been discussed
during his bilateral meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
He said the final decision would rest with the armed forces, based on their operational and technical requirements.
The BrahMos is a long-range, ramjet-powered supersonic cruise missile jointly developed by India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya through their joint venture, BrahMos Aerospace.
The missile can be launched from land-based mobile platforms, warships, submarines and fighter aircraft, offering precision-strike capabilities against targets at sea and on land.
For India, BrahMos is among its flagship defence exports, supporting its efforts to expand its international arms market and strengthen defence partnerships with friendly countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eppendorf invests RM190mil in Penang for first Southeast Asian manufacturing hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: German life sciences company Eppendorf SE is investing about RM190 million to establish its first manufacturing facility in Southeast Asia at Bandar Cassia Technology Park, Penang.
The investment marks a significant expansion of the company's global production network, with the facility expected to begin production gradually in 2028 and employ about 130 people by end-2029.
The groundbreaking ceremony was officiated by Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, alongside Eppendorf Supervisory Board chairman Philipp von Loeper and group chief executive officer Dr Christine Munz.
The project follows the signing of a lease agreement with Penang Development Corporation (PDC) in July 2026.
The facility will manufacture selected products from Eppendorf's Centrifuges & Instruments portfolio, catering to laboratories and scientific workplaces worldwide.
Spanning around 522,049 sq ft, the site will have a built-up area of about 172,222 sq ft, incorporating production, warehousing, offices, quality-related functions and logistics operations.
Chow said the investment would strengthen Penang's manufacturing landscape while supporting the state's efforts to diversify into higher-value industries, particularly scientific and measuring equipment.
"Today's groundbreaking ceremony marks the transition from planning to construction, bringing us one step closer to welcoming Eppendorf's first manufacturing facility in Southeast Asia to Penang.
"It also reinforces our efforts to diversify into high-value industries and strengthen Penang's high-value industrial ecosystem," he said.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the investment reflected Malaysia's growing position as a destination for high-value, technology-driven manufacturing.
He said the facility, aligned with the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, would strengthen the country's life sciences and medical technology ecosystem while supporting skilled employment, supplier development and integration into global value chains.
Meanwhile, Munz said the investment was part of Eppendorf's strategy to strengthen its innovation capabilities and make its global production capacity more resilient.
The project is the company's first greenfield manufacturing operation in more than 50 years.
She said the Penang facility would become an important pillar of the group's global manufacturing network, improving the competitiveness and flexibility of its centrifuges & instruments business.
Construction is targeted for completion by end-2027, followed by the installation of production equipment and a phased production ramp-up through 2030.
The company is also incorporating sustainability features like energy-efficient building systems, solar photovoltaic panels, electric vehicle charging infrastructure and water-retention systems into the facility, with plans to pursue Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold certification.
Eppendorf has maintained a presence in Malaysia for more than three decades, establishing its Kuala Lumpur office in 1995.
The Penang investment will extend its existing commercial and administrative operations into manufacturing, establishing a Southeast Asian production base alongside its established manufacturing footprint in Europe and the United States.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Raw chicken carried in open baskets raises hygiene concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing baskets of raw chicken being transported uncovered in the back of a four-wheel-drive along a highway has sparked concerns over food hygiene and halal compliance.
Threads user acsoneg02, who uploaded the video, told the New Straits Times that it was recorded along the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) near Pantai Dalam today.
In his post, he said he was shocked to see the chicken being transported in uncovered baskets.
"Shocked this morning to see a chicken being carried in a basket, no plastic bag at all, exposed before being sold to people to eat.
"After the halal chicken incident, I stopped eating chicken and am now willing to eat eggs every day. Today, I came across this again," he wrote.
Another user said they had resorted to slaughtering and processing their own poultry to avoid uncertainty over how the meat was handled.
"I slaughter and process it myself now. You just have to put in the effort," user sabaqhati__ wrote.
User mohdyazeedakhiar urged the public to avoid buying chicken without proper labelling and opt for trusted halal brands, even if they cost more.
Others called for the vehicle's owner to be identified, with user mohdnoor6061 suggesting that checks be made to determine whether the registration number belonged to a company or an individual.
"Try checking whether that plate number belongs to a company or an individual. Maybe we can find out who is involved," the user wrote.
"Police, detain them. This is very daring," another user commented.

Title: For a stronger safety culture, safety must become a way of life
Article:
LETTERS:
The recent spate of tragic incidents involving road accidents, drowning cases and people getting lost or injured while trekking and participating in outdoor recreational activities should serve as a serious reminder that safety remains a major concern in our society.
These tragedies, which have resulted in unnecessary loss of lives and immense suffering to families, raise an important question: Have we truly developed a strong safety culture in Malaysia?
Unfortunately, i believe we still have a long way to go.
Despite numerous awareness campaigns, safety programmes and enforcement measures, many people continue to take unnecessary risks, ignore safety precautions and underestimate the dangers associated with their everyday activities.
Whether it is driving on our roads, swimming at waterfalls, enjoying water recreational activities or trekking in forests and mountainous areas, safety must never be taken for granted.
We must move away from a culture of reacting to accidents and tragedies towards a culture of prevention. We should not wait for lives to be lost before taking action or introducing corrective measures.
What needs to be done? I would like to emphasise several important measures:
First, make safety education a national priority. Safety awareness must begin from childhood and be incorporated into our education system, workplaces and community programmes.
Children and young people must be taught to recognise risks, make responsible decisions and appreciate the importance of protecting their own lives and those of others.
Second, strengthen enforcement and accountability. Rules and regulations must be enforced consistently.
Whether involving road safety, water activities or outdoor recreational activities, authorities must ensure that safety requirements are complied with.
Those who organise recreational activities also have a responsibility to ensure proper risk assessments, safety arrangements and emergency preparedness.
Third, promote a stronger culture of personal responsibility. Every individual must recognise that safety begins with oneself.
Motorists must practise responsible driving, members of the public must observe warning signs and safety instructions, and those undertaking trekking or outdoor activities must be adequately prepared and avoid unnecessary risks.
Fourth, improve safety infrastructure and emergency preparedness. The relevant authorities must continuously review and improve safety facilities, warning systems, rescue capabilities and emergency response arrangements, particularly at waterfalls, rivers, hiking trails and other recreational locations.
Fifth, strengthen community participation. Safety cannot be left entirely to the Government or enforcement agencies.
Community organisations, NGOs, schools, employers, parents and the private sector must work together to promote safety awareness and encourage responsible behaviour.
Sixth, adopt a preventive and proactive approach. Authorities must identify potential hazards, conduct regular safety audits and address risks before accidents occur.
Lessons from every tragedy must be properly investigated and translated into meaningful preventive action.
Ultimately, building a safety culture requires a change in mindset, attitudes and behaviour.
Safety must not be regarded merely as compliance with rules and regulations or something we think about only after an accident has occurred. It must become a shared value that guides our daily decisions and actions.
We must cultivate a society where people do not take unnecessary risks, where safety warnings are respected, where individuals look out for one another and where every organisation takes its responsibility for protecting lives seriously.
As the Chairman of the Alliance for a Safe Community (IKATAN), i would like to reiterate that every life matters and every accident prevented is a life potentially saved.
Our national aspiration should be to achieve zero preventable accidents and zero avoidable loss of lives, whether on our roads, in our workplaces, in our communities or during recreational activities.
This requires commitment, cooperation and sustained action from all sectors of society.
Make safety not just a slogan, but a national mindset. Let us embrace a safety culture and make safety a way of life in Malaysia.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Chairman, Alliance For A Safe Community
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hilir Perak CDF rescuers stay on high alert amid monsoon flood risks
Article:
TELUK INTAN: More than 19 years of experience in handling flood disasters have not made rescue operations any easier, with each Northeast Monsoon season in Hilir Perak district demanding greater vigilance, preparedness and commitment.
Hilir Perak District Civil Defence Officer Captain Mohd Affindi Ishak said the challenging nature of the operations required personnel to remain on duty around the clock, working in shifts to ensure flood victims were safely evacuated to nearby temporary relief centres.
"I've been dealing with floods year after year, but it's never something to take lightly. The risks are real, and one wrong move could be fatal.
"We work around the clock in two shifts, from 8am to 8pm and 8pm to 8am, to help ease the burden on personnel involved in evacuating flood victims," he told Bernama at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall relief centre yesterday.
Affindi said his team often faced unexpected situations, with what started as routine checks sometimes turning into urgent rescue missions.
"It happened last year when we were checking the water level of Sungai Sungkai at around 10pm. The river suddenly overflowed its banks, flooding homes in nearby Kampung Batu 9.
"Alhamdulillah, we had a four-wheel-drive vehicle with us at the time, so we managed to rescue two elderly residents trapped in their home and take them to a nearby relief centre," said the father of one.
Apart from rescue operations, Mohd Affindi said CDF personnel also closely monitored water levels in high-risk areas to detect any changes and respond quickly when needed.
"Our personnel regularly check water levels in rivers and high-risk areas using special equipment to track any changes and decide what action to take next," he said.
He said personnel also assisted with operations at relief centres, looking after the welfare and safety of flood victims while ensuring a smooth registration process.
"At the centres, we make sure flood victims are comfortable, help coordinate their needs and ensure those with health problems are quickly referred to nearby hospitals or clinics for further treatment," he said.
Meanwhile, Affindi said CDF had deployed three aluminium boats, two fibreglass boats, an amphibious boat and four four-wheel-drive vehicles to monitor flood-prone areas in Hilir Perak.
He said rescue efforts were also supported by additional personnel and equipment from other agencies, including the police and the Fire and Rescue Department, to ensure operations ran smoothly and effectively.
"We have 50 CDF personnel assigned to carry out rescue operations across all flood-prone areas in the district," he said. — BERNAMA

Title: Hadi hopes BN-PN cooperation continues beyond Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA: The cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional is being strengthened as part of efforts to rebuild unity among Muslims in Malaysia, Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said.
He said the BN-PN cooperation in the Melaka election had shown more positive progress compared with their previous experiences in the Negri Sembilan and Johor elections.
He said the development also reflected growing efforts towards perpaduan ummah (Muslim unity), based on the principle of justice for all communities, with the Malays and Muslims playing a leading role.
"The cooperation between BN and PN in Melaka is stronger than what we saw in Negri Sembilan and Johor.
"Efforts towards Muslim unity are gaining momentum. This is not about Malay supremacy, but about ensuring justice for everyone, with the Malays and Muslims taking the lead.
"This is what we want to achieve. The BN-PN cooperation in Melaka will become even stronger, extending to the general election," he told a press conference after the BN and PN grand finale rally for the 16th Melaka election at Bukit Katil here yesterday.
Also present were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir.
Earlier, in his speech at the same rally, Hadi, who is also Marang member of Parliament, reminded Muslims against allowing themselves to be divided.
He used the analogy of a pestle and mortar clashing to illustrate how internal disagreements could ultimately benefit a third party.
"Muslims must not be divided, otherwise others will benefit. It is like a pestle and mortar pounding against each other. The harder they clash, the more chickens benefit.
"The chickens get to eat while we go hungry. We are fighting among ourselves.
"We must unite. Through unity, we can rebuild our strength to save the country. That is why we are pursuing this BN-PN cooperation," he said.
Hadi also expressed hope that the cooperation would continue until the next general election, indicating that the understanding was not limited to the Melaka election.
On Oct 29, BN signed a political cooperation agreement with PN to contest the Melaka election.
The agreement was signed by Asyraf on behalf of BN, while PN was represented by Takiyuddin. The signing was witnessed by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Title: #NSTviral: 'Don't eat it' — Online users rally to save parrotfish
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Social media users have urged the public not to buy or eat parrotfish, warning that the species plays an important role in maintaining healthy coral reefs.
The discussion began after Threads user firdausi_68 posted photos of several parrotfish displayed on ice alongside other seafood, as well as one of the fish cooked and served on a plate.
The user said he had tried the fish in Labuan Bajo, Indonesia, and was surprised by its taste, asking whether it was also sold in Malaysia.
Its vibrant emerald green scales may tempt tourists to buy and eat it when they spot it on display among other seafood, but the parrotfish is not meant for the dinner table, social media users have warned.
The discussion began after Threads user firdausi_68 posted photos of several parrotfish displayed on ice alongside other seafood, as well as one of the fish cooked and served on a plate.
The user said he had tried the fish in Labuan Bajo, Indonesia, and was surprised by its taste, asking whether it was also sold in Malaysia.
"Is this green fish sold in Malaysia? I ate it in Labuan Bajo and didn't expect it to taste so insanely good! Have you guys ever tried it?" he wrote.
His post drew criticism from several users, who questioned why fishermen and traders continued to catch and sell the fish.
"Why are these fish traders still selling this fish? The fishermen are just as bad. Everyone wants to profit without thinking about the impact on the sea and on humans themselves. Selfish," one user wrote.
Others highlighted the parrotfish's role in the marine ecosystem, with user yusairinanananana claiming that catching the fish was not permitted in Malaysia.
"This fish can't be caught in Malaysia, you know. Let alone eaten. Because it takes care of the coral reefs. Don't support it if anyone sells it. Poor thing," the user wrote.
Some also expressed concern over the lack of legislation protecting the species, saying fishermen continue to catch it due to demand and that consumers must boycott it instead.
"It's sad. There's still no protection act for this fish. Yes, fishermen still catch this fish because of demand, so it's up to us to boycott buying this fish," one user responded.
"This shouldn't be eaten. It takes care of the coral reefs. Without it, our beautiful and colourful coral reefs would be gone," said another.
The parrotfish, which belong to the Scaridae family, get their name from their fused, beak-like teeth, while the bumphead parrotfish, often found around marine parks in Sipadan, Sabah, is distinguished by the protruding hump on its face.
The herbivorous fish feed mainly on algae, using their exposed beak-like teeth to scrape the reef before grinding the coral up with teeth in their throats, a process known as bioerosion that helps keep reefs healthy.
