Title: Miti says it never cleared Megaspeed, Speedmatrix as Malaysia probes possible AI chip re-exports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said today it had never cleared Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd or its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd.
The ministry said it was working with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to determine whether any chips imported by the companies had subsequently been re-exported to other countries, and whether the transactions complied with Malaysian law.
Miti clarified that Speedmatrix was a tenant at data centres in Malaysia and that any verification visits conducted at the facilities were part of its routine monitoring of the sector, not an endorsement or clearance of the company.
“Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate,” the ministry said in a statement today.
It said Speedmatrix brought its own servers and AI chips into Malaysia for its operations, adding that importing AI chips into the country did not currently require a permit or licence.
However, since July 2025, companies seeking to export, re-export, tranship or transit high-performance US AI chips from or through Malaysia must first obtain a permit from Miti under the Strategic Trade Act 2010.
The ministry also warned that providing false information to Customs about such goods was a serious offence under the Customs Act 1967.
Miti said Malaysia would conduct its own independent checks based on available evidence and in accordance with domestic laws, while working with authorities in Singapore and the United States to strengthen safeguards.
It added that although Malaysia did not enforce export controls imposed unilaterally by other countries, companies operating locally were expected to take such restrictions into account when conducting international business.
The ministry also reminded companies against misrepresenting their dealings with government agencies.
“Malaysia welcomes investment in data centres and technology, but will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls,” it said, adding that stern action would be taken against any company found to have violated Malaysian law.

Title: Data centre boom prompts new safeguards as Malaysia targets 2027 for regulatory bill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Digital Ministry is currently in the final stages of drafting the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill.
The ministry said the bill aims to create a clearer, more comprehensive regulatory framework to strengthen the protection, operational resilience, and governance of data centres, in line with their importance as the nation’s critical digital infrastructure.
“In terms of timeline, the government aims for this bill to be finalised through the policy and legislation coordination process, then presented for consideration and debate in the Dewan Rakyat in 2027, subject to the government’s approval.
“Once passed and enforced, the Digital Ministry will coordinate the implementation of the regulatory framework to ensure compliance with the standards of safety, resilience and continuity of operations being set,” said the ministry in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat published on the Parliament’s website today.
The reply responded to Syahredzan Johan’s (PH-Bangi) question on the Digital Ministry’s plan and timeline to introduce a legal framework, such as the Digital Infrastructure Bill, to strengthen the security and resilience of digital infrastructure.
Meanwhile, the ministry said that up to October 2026, a total of 11 data centre projects have been approved in Kuala Lumpur, with two projects currently under construction and nine already in operation.
According to the ministry, every data centre project development application needs to obtain approval from the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF) where the assessment done includes the aspects of availability and adequacy of electricity and water supply.
“Meanwhile, based on records for the period from January 2025 to June 2026, the average actual water consumption of data centres in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor amounts to 2.4 million litres per day.
“At the same time, the water supply margin reserve in both areas is still at a good level and is sufficient to accommodate the current demand,” it said.
The written reply responded to Onn Abu Bakar’s (PH-Batu Pahat) question on the number of new data centres that have been approved, are being built and are planned to be developed in the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, and the assessment of the impact of the development of these large-scale data centres on the adequacy of electricity and water supply. — Bernama

Title: Sibu fatal stabbing: Police round up 14 more suspects as arrests climb to 23
Article:
SIBU, Nov 13 — Police have arrested 14 more people in connection with a fight that resulted in the death of a man who was stabbed in the chest here on Saturday, bringing the total number of arrests to 23.
Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said police arrested all 14 suspects at several locations around Sibu yesterday following intelligence operations.
He said all the suspects had been remanded for six days until Nov 18 to assist in the investigation.
Police received a report about the fight at about 2am on Nov 7, leading to the arrest of nine suspects aged between 16 and 42 at various locations in Sibu on the same day. They were remanded until Nov 15.
Abang Zainal Abidin said police were investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code and working to establish each suspect’s role and involvement.
He urged members of the public with information about the case to come forward to the police and refrain from speculating or spreading unverified information. — Bernama

Title: Kedah MB Sanusi’s 20-year-old daughter injured after motorcycle skids into drain near Alor Setar
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 13 — The daughter of Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor was injured in an accident near Kampung Alor Setol here yesterday.
Kota Setar police chief ACP Syed Basri Syed Ali said the 20-year-old, a student at Kolej Islam Darul Ulum in Pokok Sena, sustained injuries to her face and left hand, and was suspected of having fractured her right wrist.
“Preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred at about 4pm when the victim was riding a Yamaha X-Max 250 motorcycle from her college in Pokok Sena towards Alor Setar.
“Upon reaching the scene, she is believed to have lost control of the motorcycle, causing it to skid into a drain,” he said in a statement tonight.
He said members of the public and medical personnel assisted the victim before she was taken to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital for further treatment. Her condition was reported to be stable.
“The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says he backed Najib’s pardon application to protect every prisoner’s constitutional right to appeal
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that his decision to bring former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s pardon application to the Pardons Board in 2023 was to ensure every prisoner’s constitutional right to submit an appeal was not denied.
He said that as Prime Minister, he did not want to be seen as blocking any individual’s right to seek consideration from the King through the Pardons Board, in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Constitution.
“As the leader of the nation, the Prime Minister, I could not bear to be seen as victimising anyone under our Constitution. Every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal to the King for consideration.
“If I had not allowed it, I would have denied him his right. What right? The right to be considered by the Pardons Board under His Majesty the King. That is why I took that action,” he said.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said this when speaking at the Pesta Melaka Rumah Kita event at Taman Perdana Melaka here yesterday.
Anwar said the move was not exclusive to Najib, as the government also allows other prisoners to submit pardon applications for consideration in accordance with the established process.
“Anyone who makes an appeal, we allow them all. If they have a medical letter, a letter from the Prisons Department, and a letter for good behaviour, all of them are submitted,” he said.
Commenting further on Najib’s house arrest order, Anwar said he had expressed the view that the public might not yet be ready to accept such a decision, as the government is working to tackle corruption and did not want any perception to arise that could undermine those efforts.
However, he said the decision to grant house arrest was made upon the compassion and consent of the King after considering all factors, and the government abided by the decision.
He also explained that the Attorney-General’s action in seeking confirmation from the court on the house arrest issue was part of the necessary process, not a form of defiance against a royal decree.
At the same time, the Prime Minister said the debate over the issue should not distract young people from the principles of rejecting corruption and abuse of power, as well as the responsibility of championing the welfare of the people, particularly the low-income group. — Bernama

Title: Nearly 8,000 rescuers, 226 boats ready as Kelantan braces for North-east Monsoon floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — A total of 7,792 personnel, 226 rescue boats and 316 various types of land vehicles are on standby in Kelantan for the 2025/2026 Northeast Monsoon (MTL) to ensure that rescue and flood evacuation operations can be carried out as required.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) had also allocated RM300,000 in operational funds to the Kelantan State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) to prepare for the monsoon season.
He said Nadma had also provided two complete sets of Incident Command Post (PKTK) tents, in addition to allocating RM330,000 to the state committee to procure 22 rescue boats with engines and life jackets to strengthen operational capacity in high-risk areas.
“For the management of flood victims at temporary relief centres (PPS), Nadma has also sent 10,792 collapsible cubicle tents and 9,000 food kits, while 20,500 retort food packs will be distributed for use throughout Kelantan when required,” he said in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a question from Zahari Kechik (PN-Jeli) on Nadma’s preparedness for floods in Kelantan, particularly in settlements along high-risk rivers and areas that could be cut off by floodwaters.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said priority was given to positioning critical assets and supplies in high-risk areas to ensure rescue and relief operations could be mobilised promptly before access routes were cut off by floods.
He said personnel deployment, volunteer training and early evacuation mechanisms were also coordinated through the state and district disaster management committees, together with relevant response agencies.
In addition, he said eight Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) training sessions involving 726 participants had been conducted in Kelantan up to September to strengthen residents’ ability to take early action before rescue agencies arrived.
Nadma had also allocated RM250,000 for CBDRM programmes in Kelantan, including a programme held in Jeli on Sept 25 and 26 involving more than 200 participants from 23 villages around the Pergau Dam.
He said the Rakan Nadma volunteer training programme, known as the East Coast Disaster Coordination and Response Simulation Exercise (Eastcoord) 2026, was also held in Jeli from Sept 4 to 7 to strengthen coordination among volunteers and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in disaster response. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia willing to investigate Speedmatrix over Nvidia chip controversy if authorities make formal request
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Malaysia is ready to facilitate any formal request to investigate Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
However, he said, the government is yet to receive any such request.
“If they have a case, they come and check. No problem. We will facilitate,” he told reporters after the launch of MySaham Miti here on Thursday.
Johari said this when asked on whether the government has received a formal request to probe Speedmatrix, a Malaysian unit of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International.
It was reported that Speedmatrix, allegedly linked to the Nvidia chip controversy, might have breached the country’s export restriction.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman linked to Megaspeed International, prompting the US-based chipmaker to announce his immediate resignation as president, CEO and board member pending an independent investigation.
Meanwhile, Johari said he had raised the issue with data centre operators, drawing a distinction between using graphics processing units (GPUs) at a company’s own data centre and re-exporting the chips.
“So far I have already informed all the data centres… Is there anything wrong with Speedmatrix or Megaspeed renting the data centre? If there is nothing wrong and they buy the GPU for their own use in the data centre, then I cannot see what law that we need to use.
“But if there is a restriction in re-exporting that GPU, that is something that we need to look into,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar lands 13th spot in world’s 500 most influential Muslims list for 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked 13th in the 2027 edition of
The Muslim 500: The World’s 500 Most Influential Muslims
, published by the Jordan-based Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC).
According to the 18th annual edition accessible at https://themuslim500.com, the publication noted that Anwar assumed office as Malaysia’s 10th Prime Minister in November 2022, leading the Unity Government under the Pakatan Harapan coalition.
The report highlighted that Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, prioritised a robust digital and economic transition strategy for Malaysia under his signature Malaysia Madani framework, placing artificial intelligence, semiconductors, data centres, quantum computing, and the energy transition at the heart of his government’s strategic agenda.
“In June 2026, Anwar highlighted the energy transition as a key pillar of Malaysia’s development agenda, connecting the country’s future energy needs directly to the rapid expansion of its high-tech infrastructure sectors,” it said.
On the regional front, the publication underscored Anwar’s role as a constructive peace broker in South-east Asia, notably his diplomatic initiatives in easing tensions and building trust between Thailand and Cambodia following border clashes in July 2025.
“As Malaysia’s Prime Minister and Asean Chair, he hosted talks between the two countries’ leaders in Putrajaya that helped secure a ceasefire. Anwar helped build trust between Bangkok and Phnom Penh, reinforcing Malaysia’s image as a constructive peace broker in South-east Asia,” the report said.
In addition,
The Muslim 500
recognised Anwar as one of the world’s most outspoken heads of state regarding the Palestinian cause, maintaining unyielding state support for civilian protection and humanitarian access in Gaza.
“Taking an aggressive international stance, Anwar announced to the Malaysian Parliament that the country is spearheading a core international coalition drafting a formal resolution to expel Israel from the United Nations. Anwar reiterated that Malaysia’s absolute non-recognition of Israel is permanent,” it said.
According to the publication, Anwar’s meetings with Hamas officials, including its late leader Ismail Haniyeh, drew public pushback from Western countries. However, Anwar dismissed the criticism, asserting Malaysia’s sovereign right to determine its own foreign policy.
Beyond his political leadership, the citation traced Anwar’s early activism as founder and president of the Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement (ABIM) in 1971, as well as his career in major Cabinet portfolios, including Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister, during the 1990s.
It also highlighted his contributions to academia, noting that he had held visiting academic positions at St Antony’s College, Oxford, Johns Hopkins University and Georgetown University.
“He is a co-founder of the International Institute of Islamic Thought (IIIT) established in the United States in 1981. Furthermore, he served as the Chancellor of the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) from 1983 to 1988, and has received numerous international honorary degrees,” it said.
In the 2027 edition, the top spot is jointly held by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdul-Aziz Al-Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Pakistan’s Prime Minister Mian Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff General Syed Asim Munir, alongside Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Other prominent South-east Asian leaders listed in the Top 50 include Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at 16th place, Nahdlatul Ulama chairman Yahya Cholil Staquf (21st) and Indonesian scholar Habib Luthfi bin Yahya (31st).
Meanwhile, Palestinian paediatrician and Kamal Adwan Hospital director Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, who had been held in Israeli detention without charge since December 2024, was named The Muslim 500’s Man of the Year for 2027 and ranked 50th on the list. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji says Sabah welcomes tech investors, but warns big projects must protect water and power supplies
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 13 — The Sabah government is open to credible investments in the technology sector, including the development of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, but every investment proposal must undergo rigorous evaluation to ensure that the interests of the people and the state’s basic infrastructure requirements are not compromised.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the state government’s openness to investments and strategic partnerships must be accompanied by due diligence and responsible decision-making, particularly for large-scale projects requiring substantial energy and water resources.
“However, this openness must always be accompanied by due diligence and responsible decision-making processes,” he said in a statement issued by the Chief Minister’s Department Media and Communications Office today.
The statement was issued in conjunction with the signing ceremony of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the proposed establishment of Sabah’s first Artificial Intelligence Data Centre (AIDC) here yesterday, with Hajiji’s speech delivered by Deputy Chief Minister II and Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.
Hajiji said the signing of the MoU between North AIDC Sdn Bhd and several global partners was an encouraging initial step, but the project’s actual success would depend on careful planning, comprehensive evaluation and the benefits it could bring to Sabah.
“However, the true measure of progress is what happens after this signing, namely careful planning, proper evaluation and meaningful outcomes for Sabah,” he said.
Hajiji stressed that the signing of an MoU did not mean that a project had obtained state government approval, adding that every proposal must still fulfil all conditions and requirements stipulated by the relevant agencies.
He said the evaluation of proposed data centre developments must take into account technical and financial viability, electricity and water supply requirements, cooling technology, environmental protection, land use and connectivity.
He said developers must also work closely with authorities and utility providers to ensure that the development of such facilities did not undermine the reliability of essential services required by the people.
“Modern digital economies should strengthen Sabah’s infrastructure, rather than place unnecessary additional pressure on it,” he said.
Meanwhile, Hajiji said data centre development could create opportunities for local companies in engineering, construction, telecommunications, logistics and support services, particularly during the construction phase.
In this regard, he encouraged project developers to provide opportunities for local contractors, collaborate with universities and technical institutions, and introduce apprenticeship programmes to enable Sabah’s youth to acquire skills in the digital technology sector.
Hajiji said developments in AI and cloud computing offered Sabah opportunities to strengthen its participation in the digital economy, but these efforts must go hand in hand with addressing basic infrastructure problems still faced by some residents of the state.
He added that the experience of other states, including Johor in data centre development, could serve as a guide, particularly in utility management, environmental protection and the interests of local communities. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says second phase of refugee registration programme could roll out soon for UNHCR cardholders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The government is expected to launch the second phase of the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme soon, targeting United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders not held at Immigration Detention Depots (DTIs).
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the programme to register Myanmar refugee communities nationwide remained in its first phase, targeting individuals at Immigration Detention Depots (DTIs).
“The government is also studying whether movement controls should be imposed on these groups, while considering national security and sovereignty interests as well as human rights,” he said in a written reply posted on the Parliament website.
He was responding to a question from Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) on the status of preparing and presenting a comprehensive refugee management plan to the Cabinet, as well as a proposal to table the policy framework in the Dewan Rakyat.
Ahmad Zahid said the National Security Council (MKN), Prime Minister’s Department, was working closely with relevant ministries and agencies to hold engagement sessions to obtain feedback and formulate appropriate measures to address issues concerning refugees in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, in response to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau), Ahmad Zahid said refugees had entered Malaysia through syndicates at land and sea borders rather than through authorised or gazetted International Entry Points.
He said the government was also stepping up efforts to strengthen MKN Directive No. 23 on the Policy and Mechanism for the Management of Refugees and Asylum Seekers (2023 Revision), which the Prime Minister signed on June 14, 2023.
He said coordinated operations involving security agencies, enforcement bodies and local authorities were also being conducted to tackle violations by foreign migrants, including gang-related activities.
“The implementation of the DPP for registration purposes, together with integrated operations by security and enforcement agencies, is expected to help curb negative influences aimed at manipulating existing communities,” he said.
The Deputy Prime Minister was replying to Shahidan’s question on action taken by the government to tackle the entry of Myanmar refugees allegedly involved in gang-related activities, especially at Selayang Market, and measures to prevent the exploitation of the community. — Bernama

Title: Nacsa on amber alert, but Fahmi says no worrying cyber incidents confirmed so far
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that based on daily reports received from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), no particularly worrying cybersecurity incidents had been confirmed so far.
He said Nacsa’s readiness level was currently at amber alert, or moderate, following claims of cyberattacks circulating on social media recently.
Fahmi said Nacsa had looked into the claims of cyber intrusions but had yet to establish the authenticity of the alleged incidents.
“I receive daily reports from Nacsa and so far, the agency has not reported any particularly worrying incidents. However, Nacsa’s readiness level is at what is known as amber alert, which indicates a moderate level of preparedness.
“So far, there have been claims of cyberattacks and intrusions, but Nacsa has informed me that there is no confirmation of the incidents being circulated on social media. Should anything happen, Nacsa would certainly be the official source of information. So far, there has been no such confirmation,” he said.
Fahmi, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) Communications Director, said this when attending a walkabout with PH candidate for the Ayer Molek state seat in the Melaka State Election, Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar, at the Ayer Molek night market here yesterday.
Also present was PKR Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. — Bernama

Title: Anwar wants another sit-down with Loke before deciding on Transport Minister’s resignation
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to hold further discussions with Anthony Loke over the Seremban MP’s resignation as Transport Minister.
Anwar said he had yet to make a decision on Loke’s resignation letter, which he had received earlier, as he wanted to discuss the matter with him first.
“Yes, Loke did write to me tendering his immediate resignation, but as Prime Minister, I have not accepted it.
“For now, he wants to take a short break, and that is fine. But we need to discuss his resignation again,” he said at the Grand Finale of the Melaka PH Rumah Kita tour in Bukit Baru here today.
Anwar said Loke had a clean and trustworthy track record in government and had worked hard to introduce various initiatives at the Transport Ministry for the benefit of the people.
“We appointed Loke as a minister because he is trustworthy and clean. He works hard and has put forward many proposals, projects and programmes to make travel easier for the public and taxi drivers.
“He is among the hardest-working ministers and is well regarded by ministry officials. That is why I said it is strange that people want a good minister like him to step down, while asking those who perform poorly to stay on. What kind of upside-down world is this?” he said.
On Tuesday, Loke announced that he was resigning with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
The court ordered that Najib, 73, serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta, with immediate effect.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after setting aside an order issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court Criminal Registry on Nov 6.
Under the new order, Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, before returning to Kajang Prison on Aug 24, 2028, to serve his sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar hits back at claims he defied King over Najib’s house arrest controversy
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied allegations that he or the government had acted against the wishes of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia over the issue of implementing house arrest for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said his administration had always upheld the constitutional monarchy system and adhered to established legal processes.
Anwar said the decision to place him under house arrest did not fall within his authority as Prime Minister, while the Attorney-General’s decision to bring the matter to court aligned with his responsibility to uphold the rule of law.
“They accused me of being disloyal to the King. I am the Prime Minister, and the King called me this afternoon. We have a good relationship.
“…Datuk Seri Najib has been in prison for four years; to allow him to serve his sentence under house arrest is not within my authority. My authority is governed by the law,” he said at the “Ngopi Santai” programme held in conjunction with the 16th Melaka state election in Ayer Molek here yesterday.
The Kuala Lumpur High Court on Tuesday ordered Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here, with immediate effect.
Meanwhile, Anwar said sound governance, free from leakages and corruption, had enabled the government to channel various forms of assistance directly to the people.
He said this included an allocation of RM16 billion for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programmes, RM18 billion for this year’s public service salary adjustment, as well as RM200 in schooling assistance next year.
At the programme, Anwar also urged voters in the Ayer Molek state constituency to give PH candidate Muhammad Hakimin a chance to serve as their elected representative in Saturday’s 16th Melaka state election. — Bernama

Title: MediAsas: What Malaysians need to know about the new basic medical insurance plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Malaysians struggling with rising medical insurance premiums may have a more affordable option when MediAsas, a basic medical insurance and takaful plan, is rolled out nationwide in late January 2027.
Developed to widen access to basic medical protection, the plan will be supported by financial incentives announced under Budget 2027 to encourage more people to obtain coverage.
The measures are particularly relevant to workers whose employers do not provide medical insurance and policyholders finding it increasingly difficult to maintain their existing coverage because of rising premiums.
Here is what consumers should know about MediAsas and the additional measures introduced under Budget 2027.
Can existing medical insurance policyholders switch to MediAsas?
Yes, existing medical insurance and takaful policyholders can switch to MediAsas with their current insurer or takaful operator without undergoing fresh medical underwriting or serving new waiting periods.
This could be particularly useful for policyholders facing higher premiums following medical insurance repricing who want to retain medical protection but can no longer afford their existing coverage.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) has encouraged existing policyholders to maintain their current policies until MediAsas becomes available, allowing them to consider switching if they wish.
Interim measures introduced by BNM currently limit annual premium adjustments arising from medical claims inflation to no more than 10 per cent for most policyholders, with these measures remaining in place until the end of 2026.
However, the 10 per cent limit applies specifically to adjustments arising from medical claims inflation and does not cover all possible reasons for premium increases.
The option to switch without fresh underwriting is intended to make it easier for existing customers to move to a more affordable basic plan without another assessment of their medical condition, although they must remain with the same insurance or takaful operator.
What makes MediAsas different from conventional medical insurance?
Unlike conventional medical insurance products, MediAsas is designed around a standardised package of medical protection, with participating insurers and takaful operators offering the same basic benefits and policy terms to make coverage easier to compare.
The plan is offered as a standalone product and is not linked to investment products.
Its annual coverage limit is RM100,000, rising to RM150,000 for individuals aged 61 and above.
A Standard-Plus option is also proposed, with a higher annual limit of RM300,000, although this comes with a higher deductible and lower premiums.
The coverage is designed to include common medical treatments and services such as hospital room and board, surgical procedures, hospital supplies, medication, day surgery, selected outpatient treatments and pre- and post-hospitalisation services.
Proposed outpatient coverage includes treatment for dengue, influenza A and B, bronchitis, pneumonia and bronchopneumonia, subject to final confirmation by BNM.
Individuals can purchase the plan up to the age of 70, with protection extending until they reach 85.
How does MediAsas intend to keep premiums affordable?
Besides standardising coverage, MediAsas incorporates cost-control measures intended to help keep premiums more stable over time.
One is a tiered co-payment arrangement, under which patients bear part of their medical costs through deductibles and, in certain circumstances, additional co-payments.
Under BNM's proposed arrangement, the Standard plan has a deductible of RM500 per disability, rising to RM1,000 for individuals aged 61 and above.
Patients receiving treatment at designated in-network hospitals will not have to pay an additional percentage-based co-payment.
However, those seeking treatment at out-of-network hospitals will have to bear a 20 per cent co-payment, capped at RM3,000 per disability, on top of the deductible.
For the Standard-Plus option, BNM's white paper identifies a higher deductible of between RM10,000 and RM15,000 as being considered.
A higher deductible means policyholders pay more of the initial medical costs themselves, allowing the plan to offer lower premiums while providing protection against larger hospital bills.
MediAsas will also progressively adopt the Diagnosis-Related Group (DRG) payment system.
Under this approach, hospitals receive a fixed payment for each patient episode based on standard diagnosis and treatment codes, rather than billing separately for every individual service.
The intention is to encourage hospitals to manage treatment costs while ensuring patients receive appropriate care.
BNM has published indicative monthly premium ranges for different age groups and coverage options, but these are preliminary estimates, with final premiums expected to be announced closer to the plan's launch in 2027.
Figures are indicative target premiums for selected age groups, not confirmed prices.
Actual premiums will depend on factors including age, gender and health status, and will be subject to periodic reviews based on claims experience, medical inflation and any changes to the benefits covered.
What financial assistance does Budget 2027 offer?
Although MediAsas was developed before Budget 2027, the latest Budget introduced financial measures intended to make coverage more accessible and affordable.
These include:
EPF savings:
Members below 55 will be allowed to use their Akaun Sejahtera savings to pay MediAsas premiums.
SME premium subsidy:
The government will subsidise RM200 of the first-year premium for each eligible employee at small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with fewer than 75 workers, capped at 50 employees per company.
RM40 million allocation:
The government has allocated RM40 million to encourage medical coverage among employees of SMEs with fewer than 75 workers, particularly those with limited or no existing medical insurance or takaful protection.
Tax relief:
According to the Finance Ministry, premiums or contributions paid for MediAsas coverage purchased for individuals and their immediate family members will qualify for income tax relief.
The SME subsidy is expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers, particularly employees whose companies do not currently provide medical insurance as part of their employment benefits.
Who is eligible for MediAsas?
MediAsas is a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan intended for Malaysians seeking access to private healthcare protection but who may find conventional medical insurance too expensive.
It is aimed at people who are currently uninsured as well as those looking for a more affordable alternative because of rising premiums or changes in their financial circumstances.
The plan is not a social insurance scheme and does not replace the public healthcare system, which will continue providing universal access to healthcare for Malaysians.
Those who require more extensive protection can continue to purchase other medical insurance products offering higher coverage limits and additional benefits.
When can Malaysians sign up?
MediAsas is scheduled for nationwide rollout in late January 2027.
A pilot programme involving six insurance and takaful operators and selected hospitals in the Klang Valley ran from the end of July until October 2026 to test operational arrangements, customer experience and implementation readiness.
The participating insurers and takaful operators will be announced closer to the nationwide rollout.
For consumers, the plan's affordability will depend not only on its premiums but also on its coverage limits, deductible requirements, co-payment arrangements and the hospitals available within its network.

Title: Can an ageing Malaysia take inspiration from super-aged Japan’s LTC insurance?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — It is very likely that a significant proportion of Malaysians will need long-term care as Malaysia becomes an aged nation in 2048 — just 22 years away — when one in every seven Malaysians will be at least 65 years old.
Before that, can we put in place a long-term care insurance? And what can we learn from super-aged Japan’s experience?
In 2000, Japan introduced its national long-term care insurance via a mandatory social insurance system, and was described by the International Labour Organization (ILO) as the first in Asia to do so.
Here’s a summary of how it works (based on information mostly from Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and other resources such as the Global Observatory of Long-Term Care, Japan Care Concierge and the Japan International Cooperation Agency):
1. Who must contribute and be covered by this insurance?
When they turn 40, Japan’s residents (both citizens and non-citizens) are automatically included in this insurance and must start paying premiums.
2. How is the insurance funded?
The insurance cost is split in half between:
the government via tax revenue (with the municipal, prefectural and national governments sharing the bill); and
residents via insurance premiums (27 per cent from those aged 40 to 64, and 23 per cent from those aged 65 and above).
The premium amount depends on your income and your municipality, with low-income earners paying less than the standard rate and higher-income persons paying more.
Apart from the premium, you also have to pay between 10 to 30 per cent of the care services bill. This co-payment will kick in only when you use the insurance for care services.
3. Conditional care coverage if below 65; care for 65 onwards not limited to 16 diseases
If you are aged 40 to 64, the insurance will pay for your support or long-term care needs, only if it is due to 16 age-related diseases.
For those aged 65 or older, you will have insurance coverage as long as you are certified to need support or long-term care, even if it is not due to any of the 16 diseases.
4. Assessment of whether you need care services
To get the insurance to cover your care or support services, you will first need to apply to be certified as requiring such care.
Officers from your municipal government will visit your home to evaluate your physical and mental condition, and your primary doctor has to provide a written opinion of your condition to the municipal government.
A committee of experts will then decide whether you need care and what care or support level you are in.
5. What level you are will decide what services you can get under insurance
In total, there are seven categories which a person can possibly fall under, which comes with different maximum limits on the monthly care costs that the insurance covers.
There are also different support and care levels stated.
6. Co-payment comes with a cap
When you use care services, you still have to share the bill by paying out of your own pocket: 10, 20 or 30 per cent of the care costs (depending on your income level).
Based on your income and age, there will be a maximum limit on the co-payment amount you have to pay.
Picture in Ipoh, Perak for illustration purposes. Preventive care such as community-led exercise classes could help older persons continue to live in their communities as they grow older. — Picture by Farhan Najib
7. Beyond just money: Having a complete system within the community to support ageing in place
Apart from featuring insurance, Japan’s long-term care system also requires municipal governments to set up a “Community-based Integrated Care System”.
The system aims to provide services accessible within 30 minutes’ walk from older persons’ residences in communities — such as medical care, nursing care, support for daily lives, activities to prevent frailty and long-term care, and to enable continued active and healthy living.
At the recent National Long-Term Care Financing Dialogue 2026 held here, healthcare consultancy Mediva Inc CEO Kanoko Oishi said these three concepts are linked to the long-term care system in Japan: maintaining older persons’ dignity, independence and ability to continue living where they spent their whole lives.
For example, instead of thinking of using wheelchairs immediately for an older person, she said the thought process would be: “If that person can walk a little bit, how can we support them [so] that they can walk more? Or how can we support [so] that they can take care of themselves? So keeping that independence of the elderly is a very important concept.”
Mediva Inc founder Kanako Oishi also said avoiding frailty and addressing chronic diseases would help older persons stay independent, adding that Japan has a mandatory health check at age 40 along with mandatory counselling to change eating and exercise habits. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
8. Keeping it sustainable: Costs and manpower
Based on ILO’s profile on Japan’s long-term care insurance, the government had introduced measures to cope with rising costs, including by introducing higher co-payment levels for higher-income persons from 2015 onwards (20 per cent) and from 2018 (30 per cent).
According to ILO, Japan had previously tried addressing its shortage of care workers by improving pay via subsidies; expanding training and certification programmes; and accepting migrant workers.
News reports indicate that the shortage is an ongoing problem, and that Japan is currently studying plans to increase premiums for high-income earners aged 65 and above.

Why Malaysia should have national long-term care insurance and how it can be funded

Title: PKFZ ready to open records, facilitate audits amid cooking oil traceability concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) says it is prepared to provide relevant reports and facilitate regulatory audits amid concerns over the origin, authenticity and traceability of cooking oil products allegedly blended before being re-exported under Malaysian labels.
PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone would extend its full cooperation to the relevant authorities.
“We will provide our full cooperation and assistance, including making available relevant reports and facilitating any audit requests,” he said in a statement.
Lim said PKFZ operated under the Free Zones Act, while enforcement involving product authenticity and regulatory compliance fell under the jurisdiction of the relevant government agencies.
These include the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), SIRIM, the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB).
His response follows concerns raised last week by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan Ramasamy over the alleged blending of imported cooking oil with locally produced supplies before it is exported under Malaysian labels.
Jeyenderan said the alleged practice, which industry players have described as an oil “cocktail”, warranted closer scrutiny by the authorities, particularly over product origin, quality and food safety.
His remarks came after
The Edge
reported on Nov 4, citing industry sources, that imported palm oil was allegedly being blended with local supplies before being re-exported, potentially allowing foreign-origin oil to be marketed as Malaysian palm oil. According to the report, blending ratios of 75:25 or 80:20 were circulating in the market.
Jeyenderan said an examination of cargo manifests and bills of lading had raised concerns over how the oil’s country of origin was declared and how its actual composition was verified after blending.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, said independent laboratory tests were needed to establish whether the imported oil and the final blended product met the required quality and food safety standards.
He also questioned whether oil samples were tested before the vessels carrying the cargo left Malaysian waters, claiming the vessels concerned were not equipped with specialised laboratory facilities or qualified chemists to carry out detailed analyses.
Jeyenderan said any possibility of contamination should be investigated through scientific testing rather than assumptions.
“If the oil is contaminated, what could be the impact on public health? Who is responsible for ensuring that the final product is safe for consumption?” he had asked previously.
He said international rules already set clear expectations on origin, testing and traceability.
Under the Codex Alimentarius, the international food standards adopted by the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization and World Health Organization, the General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods requires a food’s country of origin to be declared if leaving it out would mislead or deceive consumers.
“Codex only allows the origin to shift when processing changes the nature of the food. Simply mixing imported oil with Malaysian oil does not change its nature, so declaring the blend as wholly Malaysian may mislead buyers,” he was quoted saying.
On testing, he noted that international palm oil trade contracts under FOSFA International, including FOSFA Contract No. 81 issued jointly with the Palm Oil Refiners Association of Malaysia (PORAM), require independent analysis by qualified surveyors.
He also warned that Article 3 of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which will apply to large operators from December 30, 2026, requires palm oil entering the EU to be traceable to the plots of land where it was produced.
He urged the authorities to clarify the procedures governing the import, blending, sampling, quality certification and re-export of cooking oil, including which agencies are responsible for monitoring each stage.
He said proper documentation and independent laboratory testing were essential to ensure that products exported from Malaysia complied with the required standards and that their country of origin was accurately declared.
He added that failing to address the concerns could affect consumer confidence and Malaysia’s reputation as a food exporter.

Title: Najib’s house arrest: Malaysian Bar entitled to challenge Pardons Board decision, says Azalina
Article:
BANGI, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has the right to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bar is entitled to mount such a challenge if it believes it has grounds to question the decision.
“But I have always stressed that when we speak of matters under Article 42, it is considered what is referred to as the prerogative of mercy, which we know is among the powers fully vested in the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the power of pardon.
“So it is up to the Malaysian Bar as to what it wants to bring... If the Malaysian Bar feels it has the right to question any issue, that is its right,” she told reporters here today.
She said this after the certificate presentation ceremony for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and Mediator Appointment Certificates, as well as the launch of the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, Legal Aid Department 2026.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) today objected to the Malaysian Bar’s bid to challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.
Senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly@Arwi informed High Court Judge S. Indra Nehru today that the AGC had received the Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review by email two days earlier and needed time to file written submissions.
Meanwhile, Najib’s lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee informed the court that his client also intended to file written submissions, as any decision by the court after leave is granted could affect him.
Lawyer Zainur Zakaria, representing the Malaysian Bar, did not object to the requests by the AGC and Najib’s lawyers for time to file their respective written submissions.
Judge Indra Nehru fixed March 17 next year to hear the application and directed both parties to file their respective written submissions by December 14, with replies to be filed on or before December 28.
On November 10, the Bar filed the judicial review application naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), the Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents. — Bernama

Title: KTMB: MyKomuter50 pass activation begins Nov 16, offering 30 days of unlimited travel on selected routes from Dec 1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The public can start activating the MyKomuter50 Pass on November 16 to enjoy unlimited travel for 30 days on selected KTM Komuter services for RM50, with savings of up to 88 per cent, effective December 1.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said the pass, aimed at easing the cost of living, was particularly beneficial to those commuting to work and educational institutions.
For example, users travelling on the Tanjung Malim-KL Sentral route, who would normally spend RM416 on fares over 30 days, would only need to pay RM50 with the pass, saving RM366 or nearly 88 per cent.
“For the Alor Setar-Butterworth route, users can save up to RM234, or about 82 per cent, compared with the estimated regular fare of RM284 over the same period and frequency of travel,” KTMB said.
The pass is open to Malaysian citizens aged seven and above who are not holders of the MyRailLife Pass. Applicants must present their MyKad or MyKid for eligibility verification.
Verification can be done through the KTM Mobile or KITS Style applications by uploading a copy of the identification document, a process that may take up to three working days.
Alternatively, users can obtain immediate verification at ticket kiosks or counters at KTM Komuter stations.
KTMB said activation and purchase facilities would be available at 34 selected stations, comprising 10 KTM Komuter Northern Sector stations, 20 Klang Valley KTM Komuter stations and four Southern Shuttle stations. An additional 11 registration counters would also be provided.
The pass is available at RM50 for each of the three service categories, namely MyKomuter50 Northern Sector, MyKomuter50 Klang Valley and MyKomuter50 Southern Shuttle.
KTMB encouraged users to complete the eligibility verification, activation and purchase processes on the same day.
Further information is available at www.ktmb.com.my or through the KTMB Call Centre at 03-9779 1200. — Bernama

Title: Anwar joins Pakatan campaign trail in Melaka ahead of Saturday’s state polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 12 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined the coalition’s campaign trail in Melaka today as campaigning intensified ahead of Saturday’s state election.
The prime minister, who is also PKR president, began his campaign activities with a walkabout at shoplots and hawker stalls in Taman Krubong Jaya at about 6pm.
Accompanied by PH’s candidate for the Paya Rumput state seat, Datuk Azman Abidin, Anwar spent around 30 minutes mingling with hawkers, traders and residents, many of whom took the opportunity to greet him and take photographs.
He then proceeded to Kampung Machap Baru before attending the Ngopi Santai programme in Ayer Molek.
Anwar’s evening itinerary included the Melaka Rumah Kita programme at the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary service centre in Bukit Baru, followed by Melaka Rumah Kita carnival at Taman Melaka Perdana in Alor Gajah.
In the 16th Melaka polls, PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 of the 28 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five) and Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (one). Three independent candidates are also contesting.
The Election Commission has set polling for Saturday, with 687,697 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots.
For the latest news on the state polls, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s FRIM puts century-old library collection online, opening 77,600 digital files to public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — More than a century’s worth of knowledge and information on tropical forest biodiversity and science from the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) is now accessible worldwide through its digital repository, the FRIM Research Depository (FRED).
FRIM said in a statement today that the FRED portal, fully operational since last year, recorded an average of 2,885 user accesses annually and offered free registration for round-the-clock access to 160,244 metadata records and 77,600 digital files.
The digital resources include scientific articles, books, theses, journals, forest maps and newspaper clippings, benefiting researchers, policymakers, industry players, students and the public.
“This digitalisation initiative marks a transformation from the physical services of the FRIM Library in Kepong, which receives an average of 2,200 visitors annually,” the statement said.
Established before 1918 and having survived both British and Japanese administrations, the specialised library houses nearly 200,000 reference materials covering 82 subjects related to forestry and forest products.
FRIM said historical records and documents preserved in the library were also among the key contributors to FRIM’s recognition as a Unesco World Heritage Site.
“To ensure authoritative and systematically organised scientific references, the library’s collection is managed using the Global Forestry Decimal Classification (GFDC), an international hierarchical classification standard also adopted by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the International Union of Forest Research Organisations (IUFRO),” the statement said.
Besides preserving heritage manuscripts from physical deterioration, the library houses four major special collections, namely the Rattan Collection, Bamboo Collection, Asean Collection and FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection.
According to FRIM, the Rattan Collection was developed in 1988 through the Rattan Information Centre (RIC), with funding from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA), to promote rattan species such as Calamus manan as a scientific commodity and support rural economies.
The Bamboo Collection, established in 1993, contains more than 1,200 reference materials on bamboo research and industry, while the Asean Collection comprises research reports, proceedings on traditional forest management and studies on the regional impact of climate change.
Meanwhile, the FRIRO (FRIM Research Output) Collection serves as the official repository of publications, consultancy reports and conference papers produced by FRIM researchers since 1990.
“Since the establishment of the Forestry School in 1927 and academic collaboration with the Faculty of Forestry at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) beginning in 1971, the FRIM Library has remained a cornerstone of human capital development and forestry education in the country.
“In today’s era of information overload, the FRED portal ensures that the public has access to authentic, reliable and rigorously evaluated scientific references,” the statement said.
Members of the public and the research community can explore the country’s wealth of tropical forest science knowledge through the FRED portal at
https://fred.frim.gov.my/Home/Index_v3
. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia selects Turkiye as preferred alternative missile supplier for Navy’s LCS project, says defence minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Turkiye has been selected as the preferred country to supply an alternative to Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the decision was made after the government evaluated proposals from several countries, including Turkiye, France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs.
“We have conducted an evaluation and have now reached the stage of determining that Turkiye is the best country from which to obtain an alternative to our missile.
“We will engage with the Turkish side for further negotiations so that we can finalise the matter,” he told reporters after the Defence Ministry’s 2026 Innovation Day celebration at the Mindef Auditorium today.
He said the government had also received assurances on the missile’s compatibility and integration with the ships’ systems, which would be further examined during negotiations with the Turkish company.
Mohamed Khaled said the missile from Turkiye was of the same type as that already ordered for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project, allowing supplies to be obtained earlier, as early as 2028.
He said the surface-to-surface missile had an operational range of 240 kilometres, with comparable explosive power and greater effectiveness than competing missiles.
In terms of cost, he said Malaysia would not have to bear the full cost of procuring new missiles, as part of the expense had already been absorbed under the LCS contract. Instead, the government would likely only need to cover the cost of installing the launchers and integrating the systems.
“If we did not have the LCS, we would have to order new missiles, which could cost RM700 million, RM800 million or RM900 million. Now, we do not need to spend that amount to replace the NSM,” he said.
On the procurement of the NSM from Norway, Mohamed Khaled said the project had stalled because the Norwegian government had not issued the required licence, meaning Malaysia would not receive the missiles despite having made payment for the procurement.
He said the government was now prepared to take legal action through arbitration, but was bound by several stages of dispute resolution stipulated in the contract, after initial negotiations reached a deadlock.
“We are therefore moving to the second stage, which is to establish a Dispute Resolution Committee between the two parties. If that process fails, Malaysia will proceed to arbitration, which can be held in Kuala Lumpur under the NSM procurement contract,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia was not waiting for the process to be concluded before seeking a replacement for the NSM, to ensure that the country’s defence needs continued to be addressed while the process with Norway was ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must tap China ties to grow exports and open markets for local products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Malaysia should make the most of its strong ties with China to boost exports and expand markets for local products, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen the business environment and help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) expand their reach in international markets.
“This will ensure that more local businesses benefit from the economic ties between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Anwar received a courtesy call from the organising committee of the Malaysia-China Entrepreneurs Conference (MCEC) 2026, led by its adviser, Tan Sri Barry Goh Ming Choon, to discuss plans for the 16th edition of the prestigious conference.
Anwar said the government fully supported this year's conference as a strategic platform to strengthen trade, investment and business networks between the corporate communities of both countries.
“I hope MCEC will continue to open up more high-value economic opportunities, including helping local entrepreneurs and Bumiputera companies gain a foothold in the Chinese market, particularly in the halal industry,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Twelve Filipinos, including six children, detained in Labuan immigration crackdown
Article:
LABUAN, Nov 12 — Twelve Filipino nationals, including six children, were detained for suspected immigration offences during an enforcement operation on this duty-free island early today.
Labuan Immigration Department director Mohd Redzuan Nawi said the operation, codenamed Op Sapu, was conducted from 11pm yesterday to 1.30am today, involving 15 officers who inspected 84 individuals at several locations, including a residential settlement.
He said those inspected comprised 51 Malaysians, 31 Filipinos and two Indonesians.
“The 12 Filipinos detained comprised one man, five women, four boys and two girls, all suspected of offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Redzuan said two witness summonses were also issued to assist investigations.
Those detained are being held at the Labuan Immigration Depot and Labuan district police headquarters for further investigation and action.
Mohd Redzuan said the department would continue enforcing the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966, Immigration Regulations 1963 and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Atipsom).
He also warned that action would be taken against anyone found employing or harbouring undocumented migrants.
Members of the public with information on illegal immigrants can contact the department at 087-421 296, submit complaints through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) at https://imi.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do, or email pro_labuan@imi.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Consumers in Malaysia may soon be able to check chicken’s halal status under proposed new rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) is prepared to introduce regulations under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 to enable consumers to check the sources of slaughterhouses and the halal certification status of chicken sold in the market.
Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was among efforts to strengthen protection for Muslim consumers following concerns raised by members of parliament over the monitoring and transparency of the halal status of chicken supplies.
He said KPDN also agreed with a proposal by Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) that responsibility for ensuring the integrity of the halal supply chain should not rest solely with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and state religious authorities, but should also involve KPDN in enforcement and local authorities (PBT) in monitoring business premises.
“Therefore, KPDN will propose better coordination with state religious authorities, local authorities and the Health Ministry to improve the monitoring of slaughterhouses and chicken sales premises,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates at the committee stage for the ministry.
On the proposal to restrict eligibility for purchasing packet cooking oil to recipients of the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance, Armizan said it was a good suggestion, but its implementation would need to be phased in to avoid affecting small traders, including night market vendors.
He said the government first needed to stabilise the implementation of targeted diesel and petrol subsidies before considering more comprehensive reforms to subsidies for other essential goods.
On the Electronic Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme (eCOSS), Armizan said the system enabled the government to obtain more comprehensive data on the supply, sale and purchase of packet cooking oil, helping it determine quota reductions and better target subsidies based on actual data.
“eCOSS was introduced in May 2023 to monitor the distribution of subsidised packet cooking oil from repackagers to wholesalers and retailers. This was followed by the Mobile eCOSS application, which records consumers’ purchase details through QR code scanning,” he said.
Earlier, during the debate, several MPs raised concerns about enforcement at chicken slaughterhouses whose halal status was in doubt, following a recent raid on a slaughterhouse in Puchong that led to the seizure of 6.5 tonnes of raw chickens and the arrest of 12 foreign workers.
Among them was Idris, who stressed that the issue should not be viewed from a political perspective but treated seriously, as it could undermine consumer confidence in the halal status of food products in the country.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) proposed that the ministry consider issuing Budi Madani petrol and diesel sales permits to selected grocery shops in remote areas, as well as providing MyKad verification terminals to allow eligible residents to access subsidies without compromising efforts to prevent leakages.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved KPDN’s 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates totalling RM2,366,037,400, with a majority vote after 17 MPs took part in the debate. — Bernama

Title: Four foreigners arrested over robbery, assault of cop in Penang; remanded for six days until Nov 17
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — Penang police have arrested four Pakistani nationals, including two women, to assist in investigations into a robbery in which a 43-year-old policeman was injured by suspects armed with sharp objects near a petrol station in Permatang Pauh on Tuesday.
Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the four suspects, aged between 23 and 36, had been remanded for six days until November 17 to facilitate investigations.
“Police are conducting further investigations into the incident. All four suspects were arrested in two raids in Kuala Lumpur yesterday afternoon and early this morning,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 394 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt while committing robbery.
The policeman was injured after being robbed by four suspects armed with sharp objects near the entrance to a petrol station in Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, on Tuesday.
Seberang Perai Tengah District Police Chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah was previously reported as saying that the incident, which occurred at about 11.30am, was believed to involve foreign suspects from a Central Asian country, including two women.
He said the suspects allegedly acted aggressively and used a sharp metal object to injure the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings, resulting in estimated losses of RM10,000.
The group’s modus operandi was to approach members of the public at petrol stations seeking monetary donations before carrying out robberies. — Bernama

Title: Man hanging cat from four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang sparks online outrage
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 12 — A video and an image showing a man hanging a cat by its neck from the window of a four-wheel-drive vehicle in Kluang, Johor, have sparked outrage on social media.
Several social media posts claimed the incident took place at Batu Dua, Jalan Mersing, in Kluang.
The incident was reportedly captured on video by someone in a nearby car before the footage was shared online.
The footage and image have drawn widespread condemnation, with social media users expressing anger and sadness over the apparent cruelty towards the animal.
Some also questioned why no one had intervened to confront the driver or rescue the cat.
It remains unclear whether the cat survived or what prompted the man’s actions.
Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police had not received any reports regarding the alleged incident.
However, he said police would conduct an investigation and attempt to identify the individual involved.
The incident comes amid several recent reports of cruelty involving cats, including a case involving the alleged sexual abuse of a cat by a man in Pasir Puteh, Kelantan, last month.
This was followed by a viral video purportedly showing a child killing newborn kittens at the Seri Nilam apartment complex in Ampang, Selangor.

Title: Malaysia approves 143 posts for new Public Defender’s Office, says Azalina
Article:
BANGI, Nov 12 — A total of 143 positions have been approved for the establishment of the Public Defender’s Office, with appointments to be made as soon as possible to strengthen access to legal aid services in the country.
The office would be headed by an officer at the JUSA C level, with approval for the establishment of the posts already obtained from the Finance Ministry, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
“This marks a new chapter for the Legal Aid Department (JBG). As we discussed during the debate on amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, we looked at the roles the government should play alongside the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), as a substantial amount of government funding goes directly to YBGK.
“Now, we will establish the Public Defender’s Office to work alongside YBGK,” she told reporters after the presentation of certificates for the Professional Mediation Certification Course and appointments of mediators, as well as the launch of the Legal Aid Department’s Madani Mediation Centre Handbook 2026, here today.
Azalina said the Public Defender’s Office was part of the government’s efforts to modernise the legal aid system, moving beyond the traditional approach to provide services that better meet the needs of the public.
She said the amendments to the Legal Aid and Public Defence Act 2025, which were passed by Parliament in August last year, were expected to come into force in the first quarter of 2027.
“What is most important to me is that the public defender works closely with the existing YBGK unit, while continuing to cooperate with the Bar Council and State Bar Committees,” she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the government hoped to make mediation part of everyday practice among Malaysians through the establishment of the Madani Mediation Centre (PMM).
She said the initiative would complement the existing legal aid services provided by JBG under the Legal Aid Act by offering another avenue for alternative dispute resolution.
“With mediation, people can come to JBG to seek an alternative dispute resolution platform through the mediation services offered under PMM.
“This is a more people-centric approach as it gives parties in a dispute the opportunity to resolve their differences through mediation,” she said.
At the event, 210 participants completed six series of the Professional Mediation Certification Course organised by JBG in collaboration with Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia and the National Legal Training Institute.
The programme was funded through an allocation of RM680,000 under the 2026 Budget Initiative to strengthen mediation expertise in the public sector.
Azalina also launched the Madani Mediation Centre Handbook, developed by JBG as a key reference to ensure that case-handling procedures, professional ethics and mediation service standards are implemented systematically and consistently nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s fiscal reforms set to lower federal debt ratio to 63.7pc by 2027, says Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Madani government is committed to gradually reducing the fiscal deficit from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022 to 3.3 per cent in 2027.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the reduction in the fiscal deficit reflects the government’s commitment to strengthen the country’s financial position, thereby helping to lower the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP.
He said the ratio of the federal government’s debt to GDP, which was 65.2 per cent at the end of 2025, was projected to decrease to 64 per cent at the end of this year and further to 63.7 per cent in 2027.
“This is part of the government’s efforts to carry out fiscal reforms to ensure that the level of debt is at the appropriate level,” he told reporters at Deloitte’s 52nd TaxMax conference here today.
He said the fiscal expansion policy in Budget 2027 is key to supporting economic growth, keeping the unemployment rate low, and increasing people’s income to help households deal with the cost-of-living challenge.
Commenting on the proposed re-implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), he said the move may not be appropriate at this time, given economic uncertainty and the government’s priority to increase people’s income amid the cost-of-living challenge.
He said the government still prioritises efforts to increase people’s income, including through a minimum wage increase.
Johan said the proposal to replace the Sales and Service Tax (SST) with GST at an equivalent rate would not necessarily increase government revenue, but rather potentially shift part of the tax burden from the business sector, including exporters, to consumers.
“The Prime Minister has commented on the issue of GST and SST several times. Although GST may have its advantages, it may not be the right time at this juncture.
“There may also be some misunderstandings or misinterpretations, which are not accurate, with some parties suggesting to implement GST to increase revenue.
He said that those who propose introducing GST to increase the country’s revenue may need a higher GST rate, and that is not something the government wants at this time.
To date, Johan said SST collections stand at 3.2 per cent of GDP, the same ratio as GST collections in 2017. — Bernama

Title: Anwar chairs special meeting as Selangor steps up efforts to tackle recurring floods
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today chaired a special meeting on Selangor flood disaster coordination at Parliament House to streamline efforts to address recurring floods in the state.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting focused on four key actions, including strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving disaster management coordination by the Selangor State Disaster Management Committee.
The other two key actions involve resolving flash floods through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and studying Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) flood management best practices.
“Special attention is being given to flood-prone areas, particularly in the Petaling and Kuala Selangor districts, which recorded 1,180 evacuees at seven temporary relief centres as of November 12, 2026.
“I want every one of these actions implemented immediately, including accelerating flood mitigation efforts and upgrading drainage systems to reduce the risk of recurring floods,” he said in a social media post.
Amirudin said the meeting was also attended by state government representatives, state executive councillors, state assemblymen, district officers, and relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), DID, the Public Works Department (JKR), and the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).
Meanwhile, he said the welfare of flood victims remains a priority, including channelling the Selangor People’s Flood Disaster Special Aid totalling RM3,000 to each eligible head of household, subject to set conditions.
“I understand the people’s anxiety, especially those who repeatedly face floods. Therefore, I want every plan translated into immediate, tangible action, not just discussions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan reassigns Culture and Heritage portfolio to Zamakshari Muhamad after Kamaruddin Mohd Noor dropped from exco
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 12 — Kelantan Youth, Sports, NGOs and Community Unity Committee chairman Zamakshari Muhamad has been entrusted with overseeing the state’s Culture and Heritage portfolio.
He said the responsibility was not merely an addition to his existing duties, but a significant responsibility to ensure that the state’s cultural heritage, arts, customs and traditions continued to be preserved and passed down to future generations.
He said Kelantan had a distinct cultural identity, rich in historical values, traditions, arts and local wisdom, which formed part of the identity of its people.
“I will focus on efforts to preserve and document historical heritage and customs, as well as strengthen local arts and culture in line with Islamic principles and the values of Kelantan society.
“The involvement of the younger generation as heirs, practitioners and future custodians of culture and heritage should also be encouraged. Strategic cooperation with government agencies, cultural institutions, artists, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and local communities will also be expanded,” he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, the media reported that Ayer Lanas assemblyman Datuk Kamaruddin Mohd Noor would not have his appointment as a Kelantan State Executive Council (Exco) member renewed, effective November 9. — Bernama
